spec.title: Catch PNG and large-ID photo display filename regressions
spec.scope:
Test-only implementation: extend server/__tests__/photo-delete.test.ts with serial backend cases calling the REAL storage.atomicCreatePhoto method from server/storage.ts. Preserve all existing tests. Do not change production code, package scripts, tier workloads, gate policy, storage or upload security, migrations, browser fixtures, or the separately sealed mobile JPEG handoff and sign-in repairs. The route in server/routes.ts extracts the last extension with (originalFilename || "photo.jpg").match(/\.[^.]+$/)?.[0] || ".jpg"; this plan tests its existing .jpg and .png outputs at the storage boundary, not HTTP handler extraction. Do not copy the filename implementation into a fake storage method or derive expected values from the result under test.

## Fixture design
Use a UUID-named disposable PostgreSQL schema, following the release-schema export isolation pattern in server/__tests__/integrity-release-schema.test.ts and isolatedPool pattern in server/__tests__/routes.test.ts. Export the reviewed shared/schema.ts with the existing drizzle-kit export --sql --dialect postgresql --schema ./shared/schema.ts command under an explicit 30000 ms subprocess timeout; retarget quoted public-qualified references to the disposable schema, including foreign keys, and execute the export only there. Do not prepend enum DDL. Use a dedicated pg.Pool whose search_path is exclusively that schema, and drizzle(isolatedPool, { schema: databaseSchema }). Patch only the imported db.transaction method with the serial test context's mock facility to delegate to isolatedDb.transaction, forwarding options and callback; the REAL atomicCreatePhoto transaction callback, queries, conflict target, row update and intent consumption must execute in PostgreSQL. No other test may overlap the patch, and restore it before dropping the schema. Create session and upload-intent fixtures with matching user ownership, unique registration keys, and canonical /uploads/ object paths. The schema owns its sequences: set the isolated photos sequence via pg_get_serial_sequence on its explicitly qualified table and setval(..., desiredId, false). Never setval, restart, truncate, or insert forced IDs into shared/public tables. Insert explicit fixture session IDs 7 and 12345 in the isolated schema. Delete each case's isolated photo and intent rows before reseeding its sequence so repeated combinations cannot conflict. Do not create, upload, rename, or delete physical blobs. Assert the returned photo ID matches the seeded ID before checking its name. Keep the suite serial and bounded (120000 ms suite deadline with bounded database connection/query waits); close the dedicated pool, drop only the uniquely owned schema, release setup clients, and restore mocks in finally/after cleanup even on partial setup or assertion failure. Preserve the existing shared pool teardown. If isolation cannot be made faithful, pause and amend through the supported route rather than adding a production dependency-injection seam or falling back to shared sequence mutation.

## Planned cases
For each session ID 7 and 12345 and each extension .jpg and .png, exercise photo IDs 1, 42, 9999, 10000 and 123456. Use an explicit expected photo-token table: 1 => 0001, 42 => 0042, 9999 => 9999, 10000 => 10000, 123456 => 123456. Compose expected strings from fixture session ID, literal token and extension; do not use padStart or slice in the test oracle. Examples include S7_P0001.png, S7_P0042.jpg, S12345_P9999.png, S12345_P10000.jpg and S12345_P123456.png. In all 20 combinations, require exact originalFilename on the returned photo AND an independent SELECT through isolatedDb. Require sessionId and id to match fixtures, originalFilename to differ from the source name, and returned/persisted objectStorageKey to equal the original unique /uploads/ path byte-for-byte, not a path derived from the generated name. Assert successful registration consumes the owned upload intent. Retry the same registration and assert the same ID, exact generated filename, unchanged object key and exactly one persisted photo for that registration; do not weaken existing ownership or retry coverage.

## Detection and handoff
The literal-token oracle must fail for source-name passthrough, missing padding, zero-padding the session ID, hardcoded .jpg, four-digit truncation and display-name-based physical key rewriting. Establish this by assertion-level counterexample reasoning in the delivery handoff, or an isolated negative-control fixture confined to test data; never mutate production code or live resources to demonstrate failure. Map R1-R4 to actual case names/assertions and observed assigned-tier results. No independent verification is selected. Planning readiness is not delivered test coverage or an application-tier PASS. Subsequent implementation requires applicable owner authorization for this sealed revision and a fresh Agent-first guard.

## Regression Guard
**Self-satisfying** — The entire implementation scope is the test/check itself: server/__tests__/photo-delete.test.ts, atomicCreatePhoto exact generated filename cases for .jpg/.png with session IDs 7/12345 and photo IDs 1/42/9999/10000/123456; returned and persisted name, unchanged physical key, consumed intent and idempotent retry assertions. No separate material behavior change is included.

spec.title: Fix the mobile photo handoff test's generated filename assertion
spec.scope:
Change only tests/mobile-photo-upload.spec.ts, case 'hands a captured photo to Photos Reel and reloads its protected image @mobile-image-orientation'. Derive expectedFilename as `S${session.id}_P${String(registered.id).padStart(4, "0")}.jpg` after receiving the created photo ID. The source file remains handoff.jpg; .jpg is its registration extension. Assert the persisted originalFilename equals this exact generated display filename, not the source name, a regex, or a value copied from the response under test. The physical object path remains upload.objectPath returned by /api/uploads/direct: do not rename it or derive it from the display filename. Preserve the backend contract in server/storage.ts atomicCreatePhoto and extension extraction in server/routes.ts. Preserve all other existing metadata and journey assertions, with no early returns, skips, weakened matching, altered fixtures, or auth changes. Require one successful direct upload and registration, registered.objectStorageKey === upload.objectPath, one persisted photo with registered.id, width 37, height 23, aisle B, section 007, and the exact expectedFilename. Complete the Photos Reel journey: active strip tab, visible photo card and thumbnail, src exactly upload.objectPath, successful protected GET to that path, decoded natural dimensions 37x23, and exactly one strip card. Reload, reopen Photos Reel through the existing phone navigation, and require a new successful protected GET and the same decoded image dimensions. Re-read the API and require equality with the complete pre-reload photo array, one persisted row, the same generated filename and metadata, and an empty offline queue. Confirm uploadResponses and registrationResponses still each contain exactly one response after reload, so duplicate registration attempts cannot be hidden by idempotent persistence. Execute all downstream image/reload assertions; currently they are unverified because the filename mismatch stops this case. This repair is independent of sign-in activation work; do not repair auth failures here. Out of scope: production changes, backend naming, storage layout, upload-security changes, gate maintenance, deployment, and separate independent verification. Any material production change requires scope reassessment and supported amendment before implementation.

spec.title: Keep form sign-in from stalling before Settings opens
spec.scope:
Repair the reported intermittent session-activation timeout in tests/clerk-sign-in-navigation.spec.ts, case 'signed-out Settings entry returns to protected Settings after form sign-in'. Preserve the real email/password/challenge form journey and distinguish active Clerk session, automatic Settings destination, and local API authorization.

## Evidence and diagnosis boundary
The owner's reported 68/70 run is separate from the available playwright-report/index.html report (69 total, 69 expected, no unexpected/flaky/skipped cases; both sign-in cases passed). The available report and last-run markers do not recover the reported failure's project, exact error or stack. Do not invent that signature or call the older pass a reproduction. Recover existing redacted evidence, or reproduce through the admitted browser-tests diagnostic before attributing a root cause. Record project, case, failed stage, timing, and exact redacted assertion signature. The reported activation failure is owned repair scope, not an ignored baseline.

The current submitSignInForm fills email and password, waits at most 12 seconds for an optional verification textbox, and submits 424242 only when it becomes visible in that window. The caller then waits separately up to 30 seconds for Clerk.loaded and Clerk.session.id, then for /settings and HTTP 200 from /api/auth/user. A late challenge can therefore appear after challenge observation ended, and accepting a code can remove its controls automatically. These are candidate race boundaries, not proven causes. A failure before an active session is not evidence that fallbackRedirectUrl or local approval is broken. client/src/App.tsx already passes the allow-listed return path to SignIn.fallbackRedirectUrl.

## Repair steps
1. Run the sealed revision's Agent-first preflight with its generated TASK_ID and TASK_PLAN_FILE and test-heavy before any implementation or workload. Confirm actual owner authorization covers this unchanged split repair; preparation and guard validity alone do not authorize execution. Restore the sealed plan through gate:restore-plan in a fresh environment when needed.
2. Recover or reproduce the exact failure at the challenge/session boundary using the supported bound browser-tests diagnostic. Preserve first-failure evidence; a passing retry proves only intermittency. Do not retry the whole suite to hide a failure or use programmatic sign-in as proof of form navigation.
3. Apply the smallest evidence-supported repair. Prefer a test-local, deadline-bound challenge/session coordinator if the form helper stops observing the challenge too early: observe session activation and a supported challenge together, allow a challenge that arrives after the old 12-second window but within the activation budget, submit each challenge at most once, tolerate controls disappearing after automatic submission, and finish only on an active session. Use one finite total activation deadline (retain the current 30-second activation budget rather than stacking new waits), bounded polling/action waits and no recovery after context closure. Surface persistent errors rather than silently swallowing them. Do not add blind page reloads, repeat password submissions, provider changes or a generic outage-retry framework. If evidence instead implicates production session lifecycle, amend the concrete affected scope and boundary assertions through the supported route before editing production behavior; do not change routing merely because a session never activated.
4. Keep browser.newContext with empty cookies/origins, official testing-token routing installed before navigation, and finally context.close. Keep the real-form case independent of tests/fixtures.ts's saved owner session and ticket-sign-in recovery. Do not mutate shared storage state or substitute activateTestSession/clerkTesting.signIn for this case. Leave the separate unsafe-target test's programmatic helper and explicit navigation semantics intact.
5. If challenge/recovery helpers change, add deterministic controlled-clock/event-order browser tests in tests/clerk-sign-in-navigation.spec.ts at that helper boundary: a challenge arriving after the old observation window but within budget eventually activates; no-challenge immediate success works; disappearing controls after code acceptance do not trigger another submission; a challenge that never completes or a persistent terminal error fails within the single deadline without duplicate submissions. These tests may simulate the helper's observations but must not replace the separate real-provider form journey. Check this file is actually selected by browser-tests.
6. Deliver bounded, allow-listed failure diagnostics (stage, elapsed milliseconds, pathname without query/fragment, booleans for Clerk loaded/session present/challenge visible, bounded known error codes and HTTP status only). Limit collection to 2 seconds and serialized output to 2 KiB; diagnostic collection failure must not mask the original assertion. Never log credentials, verification input, session/user IDs, cookies, storage state, tokens, request/response bodies, arbitrary DOM text, full URLs, raw provider errors or traces containing submitted credentials. If diagnostics code changes, include deterministic assertions that sensitive sentinel inputs and URL queries/fragments never appear and truncation/collection timeout preserves the original failure.
7. Run the complete bound test-heavy workload once the coherent repair is ready. A supported filtered browser-tests run is diagnosis only and cannot establish full-tier PASS. Preserve the empty baseline catalog; classify unrelated failures honestly rather than expanding this repair or inventing exclusions. Record all not-reached/failed steps and applicable target/revision evidence.

## Out of scope
Photo filename/image/reload assertions (separate split repair), broad Clerk provisioning-outage recovery already described by task 820, provider configuration, SDK upgrades without evidence, gate maintenance, new baseline entries, production deployment and independent verification tasks. Increasing waits alone, enabling whole-suite retries, relaxing authentication/approval, or replacing the form with a testing ticket does not satisfy this repair.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** Material reliability and challenge/session-lifecycle repair: late or auto-submitted real-form challenges must not leave sign-in stuck; persistent activation failure must remain bounded and distinguishable from navigation and local authorization; diagnostics must not disclose protected inputs.
**Test location:** tests/clerk-sign-in-navigation.spec.ts — signed-out Settings entry returns to protected Settings after form sign-in; deterministic challenge/session-helper delayed-success and persistent-failure cases, plus diagnostic redaction/budget cases when those helpers change.

spec.title: Repair sharp and multer dependency vulnerabilities
spec.scope:
Execute assigned task 959: upgrade only sharp to compatible >=0.35.5 and multer to >=2.4.0 with their required native/transitive changes. Preserve HTTP multipart memory storage, 50 MiB policy, authentication, image formats, exact saved names, protected serving and local fallback. Verify disposable clean installation and native loading; capture audit delta. The valid baseline catalog is empty; known aggregate security-audit findings outside these two dependencies are not waivers and must remain failures. No deployment, architecture redesign or unrelated dependency repair.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** Reintroduction of affected image dependencies and regression in image processing, multipart rejection, cancellation and persistence safety.
**Test location:** server/__tests__/dependency-media-security.test.ts; existing tests/photo-upload.spec.ts and tests/mobile-photo-upload.spec.ts.
**What it checks:** Consumer-resolved versions reject old affected versions with safe negative controls; JPEG/PNG/WebP dimensions, crops, rotations and thumbnails remain correct; malformed/disallowed/oversized/aborted multipart input terminates without persistence/storage callbacks. Existing browser guards retain exact saved-name and protected image reload assertions. Wire the new guard into test:unit; do not duplicate or overwrite mobile assertion or naming work.

Execute assigned native task 960 exactly: patch Vite within 7.x, brace-expansion within 5.x and source-map-js within 1.x; retain existing overrides, HMR/build and Excel contracts; add consumer-relative version and bounded parser regression tests to test:unit, strengthen workbook download assertions, verify a disposable clean install and record requirement-to-result handoff. **What it checks:** Consumer-relative and all installed/locked copies reject affected versions, bounded child processes handle deeply nested braces and reject invalid indexed offsets, HMR updates before/after supervised restart, and downloaded Excel workbooks reopen with representative cells and styles.

# Minimize page-view collection and remove weak visitor identifiers

## Task identity
**Task ID:** 1bc92e1d-057b-4d8b-baa6-e75ab3ca0115
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** cc3b6bf33682701a17e89288bc1afe64d6440ac7856d0b5d6eb1ba5a2dfff15c

## Scope
Change only the existing page-view collector and its tests: normalize known routes to coarse labels, discard query/fragment and dynamic identifiers, aggregate unknown local routes as /other, reject malformed input, derive daily-scoped HMAC identifiers from the existing SESSION_SECRET with no fallback, skip collection safely when configuration is unavailable, and preserve rate limits, non-blocking responses and short-window deduplication. Extract the actual handler for injected persistence tests without a new provider or telemetry service. No historical data rewrite, database change, runtime cleanup, deployment or workload change.

**Form:** normal

**Reference:** Owner response approving the separate page-view privacy fix in the active conversation
**Owner direction:** Yes—fix collection and add regression tests
**Applicability:** Covers this collector-only privacy fix and its recurrence tests; the subsequent gate-only authorization applies separately to the completed admission repair. No existing stored data changes.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** Sensitive URLs and identifiers must not reach persistence; visitor identifiers require the server secret; failures must not block navigation; duplicate events remain suppressed.
**Test location:** server/__tests__/support-ops.test.ts
**What it checks:** Exercise the same handler installed at /api/track/pageview with recording, rejecting and stalled sinks; assert coarse path and HMAC output, daily/key separation, no persistence without a secret, malformed input denial, immediate responses, and bounded-window deduplication.

## Scope
Repair repeated approval resetting custom capabilities and approval of rejected accounts reporting unusable success. Serialize transition decisions with persistence, retain restricted defaults on genuine approvals, explicit clear-rejected recovery, reduction notifications, Admin and self-protection boundaries. Add isolated PostgreSQL persistence and mounted route regressions in server/__tests__/routes.test.ts including controlled interleavings. No promotion features, final-Admin concurrency policy, schema, Clerk, deployment or realtime eviction changes.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** Existing approval API changes authorization state and capability persistence; race safety and error contracts materially affect account access.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Assigned native task 975 in current conversation
**Owner direction:** Execute Preserve consistent approval transitions in its entirety.
**Applicability:** Same approved R1-R3 scope and intended test-standard tier; local execution admission completes the draft without widening scope.

## Pre-existing failures to ignore
None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Flaky-test rule:** A passing retry establishes intermittency, not pre-existing provenance.

## Validation
**Command:** `test-standard`
**Why:** Backend persistence and API contract changes without browser or schema changes.
**Coverage evidence:** docs/validation/manifest.json; docs/validation/manifest.json test-standard typecheck and unit-tests include server/__tests__/routes.test.ts with PostgreSQL fixtures; bound gate:run supervises all registered steps within 300000ms.; supported invocation: TASK_ID=d34e33db-d6c0-4ba1-bacb-405b5005e34c TASK_PLAN_FILE=.local/tasks/d34e33db-d6c0-4ba1-bacb-405b5005e34c.md npm run gate:run -- --id d34e33db-d6c0-4ba1-bacb-405b5005e34c --tier test-standard
**Do not switch tiers:** This task ID is strictly bound to this tier. Other tiers will block execution; changes require a supported amendment.

## Planned guard assertions
- R1 repeated approval preserves capabilities — Approve pending User, grant custom capability through supported endpoint, approve again and reread persisted capabilities; controlled blocked transition must preserve a newer grant.
- R2 rejected approval is an unchanged conflict — Reject then approve returns HTTP 409 and unchanged stored row; clear rejection then approve succeeds. Controlled intervening rejection cannot be overwritten by stale approval.
- R3 defaults and authorization boundaries remain — Genuine approval stores restricted defaults; missing, non-admin, pending, rejected and self-targeting identities stay denied; approval removal resets capabilities and notifies authorization change; Admin protections remain.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** R1 repeated approval erases custom grants; R2 rejected approval reports success with unusable access; R3 changes defaults or weakens authorization and notification boundaries, including stale-write races.
**Test location:** server/__tests__/routes.test.ts isolated AuthStorage PostgreSQL transition cases and mounted auth approval routes.
**What it checks:** Assert real stored capabilities and admission, HTTP 409 with byte-equivalent rejected state, successful clear-rejected recovery, denial status codes and notification events. Use controlled database row locks to order competing rejection and capability updates ahead of approval.

# Scope entry and detail-shot photo references to their session

## Task identity
**Task ID:** 28d4420c-0cbf-457c-90be-997a3585fab1
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** cc3b6bf33682701a17e89288bc1afe64d6440ac7856d0b5d6eb1ba5a2dfff15c

## Scope
Reject entry creation with missing or foreign photo references, reject photo PATCH with missing or foreign parents, and guard parent pin resolution against mismatched entry, detail and parent sessions. Preserve valid same-session links and unlinking. Add real HTTP and PostgreSQL regression coverage without new features.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal

state.plan:
# Fix Mobile Flow Readiness Race

## Task identity
**Task ID:** c0f0b40a-2791-4143-af29-28c643f18da2
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** cc3b6bf33682701a17e89288bc1afe64d6440ac7856d0b5d6eb1ba5a2dfff15c

## Scope
Repair only the browser diagnostic mode-entry helper and add controlled delayed-session readiness coverage in tests/mobile-photo-upload.spec.ts. Wait for rendered session controls and explicit full-mode evidence; preserve phone capture mode without clicking and enter from full mode exactly once. Keep real upload, registration, Photos Reel and protected reload assertions intact. Do not change production defaults, upload behavior, authentication, WebSockets, reconnect indicators, rate limits or project selection. Record revision-bound R1/R2/R3 results and not-reached checks.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** self
**Material scope:** false
**Rationale:** Entire implementation is browser test/helper repair and readiness coverage for otherwise unchanged application behavior. No production or gate execution behavior is modified.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Active assigned task 986
**Owner direction:** Implement the supplied Mobile Flow readiness race plan, without production behavior changes.
**Applicability:** This revision implements the exact assigned diagnostic repair, controlled readiness tests and evidence handoff; separate review and deployment are not selected.

## Pre-existing failures to ignore
None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Flaky-test rule:** A passing retry establishes intermittency, not pre-existing provenance.

## Validation
**Command:** `test-heavy`
**Why:** Only test-heavy includes authenticated phone browser coverage and real server-backed photo handoff.
**Coverage evidence:** docs/validation/manifest.json; docs/validation/manifest.json loaded by scripts/lib/tiers.mjs: browser-tests runs scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs with existing Chromium/mobile Chromium and host-selected WebKit policy. Use supported gate:run full tier and bounded step diagnostics, with unchanged project selection.; supported invocation: TASK_ID=c0f0b40a-2791-4143-af29-28c643f18da2 TASK_PLAN_FILE=.local/tasks/c0f0b40a-2791-4143-af29-28c643f18da2.md npm run gate:run -- --id c0f0b40a-2791-4143-af29-28c643f18da2 --tier test-heavy
**Do not switch tiers:** This task ID is strictly bound to this tier. Other tiers will block execution; changes require a supported amendment.

## Planned guard assertions
- R1 delayed phone readiness preserves capture — Hold only the session GET response until entry starts; assert initial absent controls, eventual Mobile Flow header/input and zero toggle clicks.
- R2 full-mode readiness enters capture once — Start a fresh session at full-mode viewport, delay session GET until entry starts; assert explicit full-mode evidence followed by capture header/input and exactly one toggle click.
- R3 real photo handoff remains covered — Keep existing direct upload and registration response assertions, saved photo dimensions/name, Photos Reel decoded protected image and reload reads; run existing browser workload and disclose failures and unexecuted assertions separately from reconnect observations.

## Regression Guard
**Self-satisfying** — tests/mobile-photo-upload.spec.ts: Controlled delayed-session cases invoke entry while the header and toggle are absent, then assert phone capture header and controls with zero clicks, and full-mode entry with exactly one click. Existing handoff retains real direct upload, registration, Photos Reel decoded image and protected reload assertions.. # Fix Mobile Flow Readiness Race

## Task identity
**Task ID:** c0f0b40a-2791-4143-af29-28c643f18da2
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** cc3b6bf33682701a17e89288bc1afe64d6440ac7856d0b5d6eb1ba5a2dfff15c

## Scope
Repair only the browser diagnostic mode-entry helper and add controlled delayed-session readiness coverage in tests/mobile-photo-upload.spec.ts. Wait for rendered session controls and explicit full-mode evidence; preserve phone capture mode without clicking and enter from full mode exactly once. Keep real upload, registration, Photos Reel and protected reload assertions intact. # Fix Mobile Flow Readiness Race

## Task identity
**Task ID:** c0f0b40a-2791-4143-af29-28c643f18da2
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** cc3b6bf33682701a17e89288bc1afe64d6440ac7856d0b5d6eb1ba5a2dfff15c

## Scope
Repair only the browser diagnostic mode-entry helper and add controlled delayed-session readiness coverage in tests/mobile-photo-upload.spec.ts. Wait for rendered session controls and explicit full-mode evidence; preserve phone capture mode without clicking and enter from full mode exactly once. **Rationale:** Repairs authenticated denial of service through unbounded retained images and overlapping native processing.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Assigned task 993 in the active conversation
**Owner direction:** Patch resource exhaustion in session label scanning without new product flows
**Applicability:** Security hardening and regression coverage within assigned scope; no independent verification selected

## Pre-existing failures to ignore
None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Flaky-test rule:** A passing retry establishes intermittency, not pre-existing provenance.

## Validation
**Command:** `test-standard`
**Why:** Backend image processing and route integration require unit regression coverage plus compiler checks.
**Coverage evidence:** docs/validation/manifest.json; docs/validation/manifest.json test-standard typecheck and unit-tests run server/__tests__/routes.test.ts including the image resource boundary tests; existing lint and runtime contracts remain included.; supported invocation: TASK_ID=d3da8c23-8f0e-4b45-a99d-44c2ba36261d TASK_PLAN_FILE=.local/tasks/d3da8c23-8f0e-4b45-a99d-44c2ba36261d.md npm run gate:run -- --id d3da8c23-8f0e-4b45-a99d-44c2ba36261d --tier test-standard
**Do not switch tiers:** This task ID is strictly bound to this tier. Other tiers will block execution; changes require a supported amendment.

## Planned guard assertions
- R1 bounded reads — Stream readers reject actual bytes exceeding the remaining budget and destroy the stream, including missing or inaccurate metadata.
- R2 image and aggregate budgets — Real Sharp fixtures reject excessive dimensions, aggregate pixels and bytes before provider work; ordinary oriented crops retain order and dimensions.
- R3 lifecycle and integration — Production scan preparation loads one photo at a time, ignores foreign-session photos, and rejects over-budget scans; shared slot rejects overlap and releases idempotently after errors. Both routes use the protected preparation and release slot in finally.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** R1 unbounded photo reads; R2 decompression and aggregate scan memory; R3 concurrent scans and resource leaks
**Test location:** server/__tests__/routes.test.ts and server/lib/labelScanResources.ts
**What it checks:** Bounded stream fixtures assert rejection and destruction, Sharp image fixtures assert early pixel and aggregate budget failures, production preparation fixtures assert crop ordering and foreign-session exclusion, and slot fixtures assert overlap rejection and release on failure. Route wiring assertions cover both protected endpoints.

spec.title: Bound label scan image resources
spec.scope: Assigned security repair: bound actual photo download bytes, image pixels and aggregate session scan resources; prepare crops one photo at a time rather than retaining all oriented photos; share a process-wide nonqueued scan slot across photo and session endpoints; preserve authorization, crop coordinates, AI batching and persistence. No upload or UI changes.
spec.why: Backend image processing and route integration require unit regression coverage plus compiler checks.
spec.coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json test-standard typecheck and unit-tests run server/__tests__/routes.test.ts including the image resource boundary tests; existing lint and runtime contracts remain included.

approval.reference: Assigned task 993 in the active conversation
approval.direction: Patch resource exhaustion in session label scanning without new product flows
approval.applicability: Security hardening and regression coverage within assigned scope; no independent verification selected

assertions.requirement: R1 bounded reads
assertions.check: Stream readers reject actual bytes exceeding the remaining budget and destroy the stream, including missing or inaccurate metadata.

assertions.requirement: R2 image and aggregate budgets
assertions.check: Real Sharp fixtures reject excessive dimensions, aggregate pixels and bytes before provider work; ordinary oriented crops retain order and dimensions.

assertions.requirement: R3 lifecycle and integration
assertions.check: Production scan preparation loads one photo at a time, ignores foreign-session photos, and rejects over-budget scans; shared slot rejects overlap and releases idempotently after errors. Both routes use the protected preparation and release slot in finally.

regression.rationale: Repairs authenticated denial of service through unbounded retained images and overlapping native processing.
regression.covers: R1 unbounded photo reads; R2 decompression and aggregate scan memory; R3 concurrent scans and resource leaks
regression.assertion: Bounded stream fixtures assert rejection and destruction, Sharp image fixtures assert early pixel and aggregate budget failures, production preparation fixtures assert crop ordering and foreign-session exclusion, and slot fixtures assert overlap rejection and release on failure. Route wiring assertions cover both protected endpoints.

state.plan:
# Restrict pin entry links and deletion to the authorized session

## Task identity
**Task ID:** 682ad15d-d101-4587-835b-17d2e936006e
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** cc3b6bf33682701a17e89288bc1afe64d6440ac7856d0b5d6eb1ba5a2dfff15c

## Scope
Task 990 only: reject missing or cross-session entryId in PATCH pins; constrain linked-entry deletion in both pin DELETE handlers to the photo session, including existing malformed links; preserve same-session links, null detachment, permissions, locks and undo tokens. Add route and real PostgreSQL regression coverage without new flows or schema migration.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** Repairs server-side object authorization and a cross-session destructive data-integrity failure.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Assigned task 990 in the active conversation
**Owner direction:** Fix the specified broken access control in pin links and deletion, without new features.
**Applicability:** The planned route and storage constraints and regression tests implement only the assigned vulnerability.

## Pre-existing failures to ignore
None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Flaky-test rule:** A passing retry establishes intermittency, not pre-existing provenance.

## Validation
**Command:** `test-standard`
**Why:** Backend authorization repair needs the API/unit suite and compiler checks; no UI or browser behavior changes.
**Coverage evidence:** docs/validation/manifest.json; docs/validation/manifest.json test-standard unit step executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts, including pin route authorization and PostgreSQL scoped-deletion cases; typecheck covers storage signatures.; supported invocation: TASK_ID=682ad15d-d101-4587-835b-17d2e936006e TASK_PLAN_FILE=.local/tasks/682ad15d-d101-4587-835b-17d2e936006e.md npm run gate:run -- --id 682ad15d-d101-4587-835b-17d2e936006e --tier test-standard
**Do not switch tiers:** This task ID is strictly bound to this tier. Other tiers will block execution; changes require a supported amendment.

## Planned guard assertions
- Cross-session and missing links are rejected — Actual PATCH handler returns 400 and never updates pin for a foreign or missing entry; same-session and null links succeed.
- Both pin deletion handlers protect foreign entries — Actual handlers pass the photo session to constrained storage deletion, and PostgreSQL tests prove a foreign entry survives a mismatched deletion while a same-session entry is deleted.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** An editor links a pin to another session's entry then deletes it, or deletes an already malformed pin.
**Test location:** server/__tests__/routes.test.ts
**What it checks:** PATCH rejects foreign and missing entry IDs without mutation; both DELETE handlers constrain linked deletion to the photo session; real PostgreSQL deletion preserves foreign entries and removes same-session entries; valid links and null detachment remain supported.

# Restrict pin entry links and deletion to the authorized session

## Task identity
**Task ID:** 682ad15d-d101-4587-835b-17d2e936006e
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** cc3b6bf33682701a17e89288bc1afe64d6440ac7856d0b5d6eb1ba5a2dfff15c

## Scope
Task 990 only: reject missing or cross-session entryId in PATCH pins; constrain linked-entry deletion in both pin DELETE handlers to the photo session, including existing malformed links; preserve same-session links, null detachment, permissions, locks and undo tokens. Add route and real PostgreSQL regression coverage without new flows or schema migration.

**Form:** normal

**Do not switch tiers:** This task ID is strictly bound to this tier. Other tiers will block execution; changes require a supported amendment.

## Planned guard assertions
- Cross-session and missing links are rejected — Actual PATCH handler returns 400 and never updates pin for a foreign or missing entry; same-session and null links succeed.

# Restrict pin entry links and deletion to the authorized session

## Task identity
**Task ID:** 682ad15d-d101-4587-835b-17d2e936006e
**Revision:** 2
**Skill pin:** cc3b6bf33682701a17e89288bc1afe64d6440ac7856d0b5d6eb1ba5a2dfff15c

## Scope
Task 990 only: reject missing or cross-session entryId in PATCH pins and POST photo pins, including new rows and draft promotion; constrain linked-entry deletion in both pin DELETE handlers to the photo session, including existing malformed links; preserve same-session creation and links, null detachment, permissions, locks and undo tokens. Add route and real PostgreSQL regression coverage without new flows or schema migration.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** Repairs server-side object authorization and a cross-session destructive data-integrity failure.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Assigned task 990 in the active conversation
**Owner direction:** Fix the specified broken access control in pin links and deletion, without new features.
**Applicability:** The assigned broken-access-control repair also covers the completion check's discovered pin creation and draft-promotion bypass of the same entry-link invariant; no new flows or features.

## Pre-existing failures to ignore
None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Flaky-test rule:** A passing retry establishes intermittency, not pre-existing provenance.

## Validation
**Command:** `test-standard`
**Why:** Backend authorization repair needs the API/unit suite and compiler checks; no UI or browser behavior changes.
**Coverage evidence:** docs/validation/manifest.json; docs/validation/manifest.json test-standard unit-tests step executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts, including pin creation, draft promotion, patch authorization and PostgreSQL scoped-deletion cases; typecheck covers storage signatures.; supported invocation: TASK_ID=682ad15d-d101-4587-835b-17d2e936006e TASK_PLAN_FILE=.local/tasks/682ad15d-d101-4587-835b-17d2e936006e.md npm run gate:run -- --id 682ad15d-d101-4587-835b-17d2e936006e --tier test-standard
**Do not switch tiers:** This task ID is strictly bound to this tier. Other tiers will block execution; changes require a supported amendment.

## Planned guard assertions
- Cross-session and missing links are rejected — Actual PATCH and POST pin handlers return 400 without any insertion or draft promotion for a foreign or missing entry; same-session creation and links and null links succeed.
- Both pin deletion handlers protect foreign entries — Actual handlers pass the photo session to constrained storage deletion, and PostgreSQL tests prove a foreign entry survives a mismatched deletion while a same-session entry is deleted.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** An editor links a pin to another session's entry through PATCH, creation, or draft promotion then deletes it, or deletes an already malformed pin.
**Test location:** server/__tests__/routes.test.ts
**What it checks:** PATCH and POST reject foreign and missing entry IDs without mutation, including draft promotion; both DELETE handlers constrain linked deletion to the photo session; real PostgreSQL deletion preserves foreign entries and removes same-session entries; same-session creation, draft promotion, valid links and null links remain supported.

spec.title: Restrict pin entry links and deletion to the authorized session
spec.scope: Task 990 only: reject missing or cross-session entryId in PATCH pins and POST photo pins, including new rows and draft promotion; constrain linked-entry deletion in both pin DELETE handlers to the photo session, including existing malformed links; preserve same-session creation and links, null detachment, permissions, locks and undo tokens. spec.title: Preserve nested folder access
spec.scope:
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope
Do not recursively delete descendants or sessions, redesign folder navigation or permissions, change retention policy, broadly harden folder concurrency, add historical-data cleanup migrations, or change the policy for individually trashed sessions when their folder is restored first.
spec.why: The defect affects persisted parent relationships and rendered dashboard navigation; both the authenticated API lifecycle and actual browser visibility are needed alongside the scheduled lower-layer and compiler checks.
spec.coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json test-heavy: typecheck checks TypeScript changes; unit-tests executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts for isolated shared expiry-deletion storage/API behavior; browser-tests runs scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs, which provisions and removes a disposable database and executes tests/folder-expand.spec.ts against authenticated folder APIs and dashboard visibility. The tier is bounded at 900000 ms. The disposable-browser-database path is required; any unavailable prerequisite blocks rather than permitting a weaker tier.

approval.reference: Assigned project Task 981 and its approved scope in the active task assignment.
approval.direction: Preserve access to surviving nested folders and sessions across parent trash, restore, permanent deletion, and automatic expiry, with cross-account isolation and actual dashboard coverage.
approval.applicability: This revision implements only the assigned Task 981 scope and binds the intended test-heavy workload. The executing Agent remains responsible for current ordinary authorization; the local guard does not authenticate native approval or lifecycle.

assertions.requirement: R1: Trashing a parent keeps its active child, grandchild, and contained sessions reachable
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested-folder trash/restore journey: create P > C > G and a session in C via authenticated APIs; trash P, reload the dashboard, and assert C and G are visible/navigable with the same session IDs and persisted parent relationships; restore P and assert its intended restoration behavior.

assertions.requirement: R2: Parent restoration does not overwrite a later explicit child move
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after trashing P and confirming C is promoted, explicitly move C to another existing folder through the folder API, restore P, and assert C remains at the explicit destination while deeper descendants and sessions remain intact.

assertions.requirement: R3: Permanent deletion and the shared expiry deletion operation promote surviving direct children safely
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — permanently delete a trashed P in P > C > G and assert C is promoted to P's former parent/root, G still points to C, and C's session IDs survive; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated database/storage case invokes the same folder deletion operation used by expiry, then asserts no child points at the removed P and deeper relationships and sessions are preserved.

assertions.requirement: R4: Lifecycle operations do not change another account's folder tree or sessions
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts and the isolated server deletion-path case — create a second account's folder/session tree as a control, run parent trash/permanent deletion or expiry for the first owner, then assert the control rows and relationships remain unchanged.

assertions.requirement: R5: Dashboard renders surviving nested descendants after parent removal
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after parent trash and after permanent deletion, reload the authenticated dashboard and assert child and grandchild folder headers and the contained session card are visible through ordinary navigation.

regression.rationale: This repairs existing persisted folder relationships and a visible dashboard failure; an active child can become unreachable and permanent deletion can leave it attached to a nonexistent parent.
regression.covers: Parent trash, restoration, explicit permanent deletion, and shared automatic-expiry deletion must preserve accessible descendants and sessions without changing another user's folder tree or overwriting an explicit later move.
regression.testLocation: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
regression.assertion: Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.

spec.title: Preserve nested folder access
spec.scope:
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope
Do not recursively delete descendants or sessions, redesign folder navigation or permissions, change retention policy, broadly harden folder concurrency, add historical-data cleanup migrations, or change the policy for individually trashed sessions when their folder is restored first.
spec.why: The defect affects persisted parent relationships and rendered dashboard navigation; both the authenticated API lifecycle and actual browser visibility are needed alongside the scheduled lower-layer and compiler checks.
spec.coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json test-heavy: typecheck checks TypeScript changes; unit-tests executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts for isolated shared expiry-deletion storage/API behavior; browser-tests runs scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs, which provisions and removes a disposable database and executes tests/folder-expand.spec.ts against authenticated folder APIs and dashboard visibility. The tier is bounded at 900000 ms. The disposable-browser-database path is required; any unavailable prerequisite blocks rather than permitting a weaker tier.

approval.reference: Assigned project Task 981 and its approved scope in the active task assignment.
approval.direction: Preserve access to surviving nested folders and sessions across parent trash, restore, permanent deletion, and automatic expiry, with cross-account isolation and actual dashboard coverage.
approval.applicability: This revision implements only the assigned Task 981 scope and binds the intended test-heavy workload. The executing Agent remains responsible for current ordinary authorization; the local guard does not authenticate native approval or lifecycle.

assertions.requirement: R1: Trashing a parent keeps its active child, grandchild, and contained sessions reachable
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested-folder trash/restore journey: create P > C > G and a session in C via authenticated APIs; trash P, reload the dashboard, and assert C and G are visible/navigable with the same session IDs and persisted parent relationships; restore P and assert its intended restoration behavior.

assertions.requirement: R2: Parent restoration does not overwrite a later explicit child move
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after trashing P and confirming C is promoted, explicitly move C to another existing folder through the folder API, restore P, and assert C remains at the explicit destination while deeper descendants and sessions remain intact.

assertions.requirement: R3: Permanent deletion and the shared expiry deletion operation promote surviving direct children safely
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — permanently delete a trashed P in P > C > G and assert C is promoted to P's former parent/root, G still points to C, and C's session IDs survive; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated database/storage case invokes the same folder deletion operation used by expiry, then asserts no child points at the removed P and deeper relationships and sessions are preserved.

assertions.requirement: R4: Lifecycle operations do not change another account's folder tree or sessions
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts and the isolated server deletion-path case — create a second account's folder/session tree as a control, run parent trash/permanent deletion or expiry for the first owner, then assert the control rows and relationships remain unchanged.

assertions.requirement: R5: Dashboard renders surviving nested descendants after parent removal
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after parent trash and after permanent deletion, reload the authenticated dashboard and assert child and grandchild folder headers and the contained session card are visible through ordinary navigation.

regression.rationale: This repairs existing persisted folder relationships and a visible dashboard failure; an active child can become unreachable and permanent deletion can leave it attached to a nonexistent parent.
regression.covers: Parent trash, restoration, explicit permanent deletion, and shared automatic-expiry deletion must preserve accessible descendants and sessions without changing another user's folder tree or overwriting an explicit later move.
regression.testLocation: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
regression.assertion: Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.

spec.regressionGuard:
**Covers:** Parent trash, restoration, explicit permanent deletion, and shared automatic-expiry deletion must preserve accessible descendants and sessions without changing another user's folder tree or overwriting an explicit later move.
**Test location:** tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
**What it checks:** Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.

spec.title: Preserve nested folder access
spec.scope:
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope
Do not recursively delete descendants or sessions, redesign folder navigation or permissions, change retention policy, broadly harden folder concurrency, add historical-data cleanup migrations, or change the policy for individually trashed sessions when their folder is restored first.
spec.why: The defect affects persisted parent relationships and rendered dashboard navigation; both the authenticated API lifecycle and actual browser visibility are needed alongside the scheduled lower-layer and compiler checks.
spec.coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json test-heavy: typecheck checks TypeScript changes; unit-tests executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts for isolated shared expiry-deletion storage/API behavior; browser-tests runs scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs, which provisions and removes a disposable database and executes tests/folder-expand.spec.ts against authenticated folder APIs and dashboard visibility. The tier is bounded at 900000 ms. The disposable-browser-database path is required; any unavailable prerequisite blocks rather than permitting a weaker tier.

approval.reference: Assigned project Task 981 and its approved scope in the active task assignment.
approval.direction: Preserve access to surviving nested folders and sessions across parent trash, restore, permanent deletion, and automatic expiry, with cross-account isolation and actual dashboard coverage.
approval.applicability: This revision implements only the assigned Task 981 scope and binds the intended test-heavy workload. The executing Agent remains responsible for current ordinary authorization; the local guard does not authenticate native approval or lifecycle.

assertions.requirement: R1: Trashing a parent keeps its active child, grandchild, and contained sessions reachable
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested-folder trash/restore journey: create P > C > G and a session in C via authenticated APIs; trash P, reload the dashboard, and assert C and G are visible/navigable with the same session IDs and persisted parent relationships; restore P and assert its intended restoration behavior.

assertions.requirement: R2: Parent restoration does not overwrite a later explicit child move
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after trashing P and confirming C is promoted, explicitly move C to another existing folder through the folder API, restore P, and assert C remains at the explicit destination while deeper descendants and sessions remain intact.

assertions.requirement: R3: Permanent deletion and the shared expiry deletion operation promote surviving direct children safely
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — permanently delete a trashed P in P > C > G and assert C is promoted to P's former parent/root, G still points to C, and C's session IDs survive; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated database/storage case invokes the same folder deletion operation used by expiry, then asserts no child points at the removed P and deeper relationships and sessions are preserved.

assertions.requirement: R4: Lifecycle operations do not change another account's folder tree or sessions
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts and the isolated server deletion-path case — create a second account's folder/session tree as a control, run parent trash/permanent deletion or expiry for the first owner, then assert the control rows and relationships remain unchanged.

assertions.requirement: R5: Dashboard renders surviving nested descendants after parent removal
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after parent trash and after permanent deletion, reload the authenticated dashboard and assert child and grandchild folder headers and the contained session card are visible through ordinary navigation.

regression.rationale: This repairs existing persisted folder relationships and a visible dashboard failure; an active child can become unreachable and permanent deletion can leave it attached to a nonexistent parent.
regression.covers: Parent trash, restoration, explicit permanent deletion, and shared automatic-expiry deletion must preserve accessible descendants and sessions without changing another user's folder tree or overwriting an explicit later move.
regression.testLocation: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
regression.assertion: Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.

spec.title: Preserve nested folder access
spec.scope:
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope
Do not recursively delete descendants or sessions, redesign folder navigation or permissions, change retention policy, broadly harden folder concurrency, add historical-data cleanup migrations, or change the policy for individually trashed sessions when their folder is restored first.
spec.why: The defect affects persisted parent relationships and rendered dashboard navigation; both the authenticated API lifecycle and actual browser visibility are needed alongside the scheduled lower-layer and compiler checks.
spec.coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json test-heavy: typecheck checks TypeScript changes; unit-tests executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts for isolated shared expiry-deletion storage/API behavior; browser-tests runs scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs, which provisions and removes a disposable database and executes tests/folder-expand.spec.ts against authenticated folder APIs and dashboard visibility. The tier is bounded at 900000 ms. The disposable-browser-database path is required; any unavailable prerequisite blocks rather than permitting a weaker tier.

approval.reference: Assigned project Task 981 and its approved scope in the active task assignment.
approval.direction: Preserve access to surviving nested folders and sessions across parent trash, restore, permanent deletion, and automatic expiry, with cross-account isolation and actual dashboard coverage.
approval.applicability: This revision implements only the assigned Task 981 scope and binds the intended test-heavy workload. The executing Agent remains responsible for current ordinary authorization; the local guard does not authenticate native approval or lifecycle.

assertions.requirement: R1: Trashing a parent keeps its active child, grandchild, and contained sessions reachable
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested-folder trash/restore journey: create P > C > G and a session in C via authenticated APIs; trash P, reload the dashboard, and assert C and G are visible/navigable with the same session IDs and persisted parent relationships; restore P and assert its intended restoration behavior.

assertions.requirement: R2: Parent restoration does not overwrite a later explicit child move
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after trashing P and confirming C is promoted, explicitly move C to another existing folder through the folder API, restore P, and assert C remains at the explicit destination while deeper descendants and sessions remain intact.

assertions.requirement: R3: Permanent deletion and the shared expiry deletion operation promote surviving direct children safely
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — permanently delete a trashed P in P > C > G and assert C is promoted to P's former parent/root, G still points to C, and C's session IDs survive; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated database/storage case invokes the same folder deletion operation used by expiry, then asserts no child points at the removed P and deeper relationships and sessions are preserved.

assertions.requirement: R4: Lifecycle operations do not change another account's folder tree or sessions
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts and the isolated server deletion-path case — create a second account's folder/session tree as a control, run parent trash/permanent deletion or expiry for the first owner, then assert the control rows and relationships remain unchanged.

assertions.requirement: R5: Dashboard renders surviving nested descendants after parent removal
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after parent trash and after permanent deletion, reload the authenticated dashboard and assert child and grandchild folder headers and the contained session card are visible through ordinary navigation.

regression.rationale: This repairs existing persisted folder relationships and a visible dashboard failure; an active child can become unreachable and permanent deletion can leave it attached to a nonexistent parent.
regression.covers: Parent trash, restoration, explicit permanent deletion, and shared automatic-expiry deletion must preserve accessible descendants and sessions without changing another user's folder tree or overwriting an explicit later move.
regression.testLocation: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
regression.assertion: Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.

spec.title: Preserve nested folder access
spec.scope:
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope
Do not recursively delete descendants or sessions, redesign folder navigation or permissions, change retention policy, broadly harden folder concurrency, add historical-data cleanup migrations, or change the policy for individually trashed sessions when their folder is restored first.
spec.why: The defect affects persisted parent relationships and rendered dashboard navigation; both the authenticated API lifecycle and actual browser visibility are needed alongside the scheduled lower-layer and compiler checks.
spec.coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json test-heavy: typecheck checks TypeScript changes; unit-tests executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts for isolated shared expiry-deletion storage/API behavior; browser-tests runs scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs, which provisions and removes a disposable database and executes tests/folder-expand.spec.ts against authenticated folder APIs and dashboard visibility. The tier is bounded at 900000 ms. The disposable-browser-database path is required; any unavailable prerequisite blocks rather than permitting a weaker tier.

approval.reference: Assigned project Task 981 and its approved scope in the active task assignment.
approval.direction: Preserve access to surviving nested folders and sessions across parent trash, restore, permanent deletion, and automatic expiry, with cross-account isolation and actual dashboard coverage.
approval.applicability: This revision implements only the assigned Task 981 scope and binds the intended test-heavy workload. The executing Agent remains responsible for current ordinary authorization; the local guard does not authenticate native approval or lifecycle.

assertions.requirement: R1: Trashing a parent keeps its active child, grandchild, and contained sessions reachable
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested-folder trash/restore journey: create P > C > G and a session in C via authenticated APIs; trash P, reload the dashboard, and assert C and G are visible/navigable with the same session IDs and persisted parent relationships; restore P and assert its intended restoration behavior.

assertions.requirement: R2: Parent restoration does not overwrite a later explicit child move
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after trashing P and confirming C is promoted, explicitly move C to another existing folder through the folder API, restore P, and assert C remains at the explicit destination while deeper descendants and sessions remain intact.

assertions.requirement: R3: Permanent deletion and the shared expiry deletion operation promote surviving direct children safely
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — permanently delete a trashed P in P > C > G and assert C is promoted to P's former parent/root, G still points to C, and C's session IDs survive; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated database/storage case invokes the same folder deletion operation used by expiry, then asserts no child points at the removed P and deeper relationships and sessions are preserved.

assertions.requirement: R4: Lifecycle operations do not change another account's folder tree or sessions
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts and the isolated server deletion-path case — create a second account's folder/session tree as a control, run parent trash/permanent deletion or expiry for the first owner, then assert the control rows and relationships remain unchanged.

assertions.requirement: R5: Dashboard renders surviving nested descendants after parent removal
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after parent trash and after permanent deletion, reload the authenticated dashboard and assert child and grandchild folder headers and the contained session card are visible through ordinary navigation.

regression.rationale: This repairs existing persisted folder relationships and a visible dashboard failure; an active child can become unreachable and permanent deletion can leave it attached to a nonexistent parent.
regression.covers: Parent trash, restoration, explicit permanent deletion, and shared automatic-expiry deletion must preserve accessible descendants and sessions without changing another user's folder tree or overwriting an explicit later move.
regression.testLocation: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
regression.assertion: Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.

spec.title: Preserve nested folder access
spec.scope:
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope
Do not recursively delete descendants or sessions, redesign folder navigation or permissions, change retention policy, broadly harden folder concurrency, add historical-data cleanup migrations, or change the policy for individually trashed sessions when their folder is restored first.
spec.why: The defect affects persisted parent relationships and rendered dashboard navigation; both the authenticated API lifecycle and actual browser visibility are needed alongside the scheduled lower-layer and compiler checks.
spec.coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json test-heavy: typecheck checks TypeScript changes; unit-tests executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts for isolated shared expiry-deletion storage/API behavior; browser-tests runs scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs, which provisions and removes a disposable database and executes tests/folder-expand.spec.ts against authenticated folder APIs and dashboard visibility. The tier is bounded at 900000 ms. The disposable-browser-database path is required; any unavailable prerequisite blocks rather than permitting a weaker tier.

approval.reference: Assigned project Task 981 and its approved scope in the active task assignment.
approval.direction: Preserve access to surviving nested folders and sessions across parent trash, restore, permanent deletion, and automatic expiry, with cross-account isolation and actual dashboard coverage.
approval.applicability: This revision implements only the assigned Task 981 scope and binds the intended test-heavy workload. The executing Agent remains responsible for current ordinary authorization; the local guard does not authenticate native approval or lifecycle.

assertions.requirement: R1: Trashing a parent keeps its active child, grandchild, and contained sessions reachable
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested-folder trash/restore journey: create P > C > G and a session in C via authenticated APIs; trash P, reload the dashboard, and assert C and G are visible/navigable with the same session IDs and persisted parent relationships; restore P and assert its intended restoration behavior.

assertions.requirement: R2: Parent restoration does not overwrite a later explicit child move
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after trashing P and confirming C is promoted, explicitly move C to another existing folder through the folder API, restore P, and assert C remains at the explicit destination while deeper descendants and sessions remain intact.

assertions.requirement: R3: Permanent deletion and the shared expiry deletion operation promote surviving direct children safely
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — permanently delete a trashed P in P > C > G and assert C is promoted to P's former parent/root, G still points to C, and C's session IDs survive; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated database/storage case invokes the same folder deletion operation used by expiry, then asserts no child points at the removed P and deeper relationships and sessions are preserved.

assertions.requirement: R4: Lifecycle operations do not change another account's folder tree or sessions
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts and the isolated server deletion-path case — create a second account's folder/session tree as a control, run parent trash/permanent deletion or expiry for the first owner, then assert the control rows and relationships remain unchanged.

assertions.requirement: R5: Dashboard renders surviving nested descendants after parent removal
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after parent trash and after permanent deletion, reload the authenticated dashboard and assert child and grandchild folder headers and the contained session card are visible through ordinary navigation.

regression.testLocation: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
regression.assertion: Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.
