spec.title: Preserve nested folder access
spec.scope:
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope
Do not recursively delete descendants or sessions, redesign folder navigation or permissions, change retention policy, broadly harden folder concurrency, add historical-data cleanup migrations, or change the policy for individually trashed sessions when their folder is restored first.
spec.why: The defect affects persisted parent relationships and rendered dashboard navigation; both the authenticated API lifecycle and actual browser visibility are needed alongside the scheduled lower-layer and compiler checks.
spec.coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json test-heavy: typecheck checks TypeScript changes; unit-tests executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts for isolated shared expiry-deletion storage/API behavior; browser-tests runs scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs, which provisions and removes a disposable database and executes tests/folder-expand.spec.ts against authenticated folder APIs and dashboard visibility. The tier is bounded at 900000 ms. The disposable-browser-database path is required; any unavailable prerequisite blocks rather than permitting a weaker tier.

approval.reference: Assigned project Task 981 and its approved scope in the active task assignment.
approval.direction: Preserve access to surviving nested folders and sessions across parent trash, restore, permanent deletion, and automatic expiry, with cross-account isolation and actual dashboard coverage.
approval.applicability: This revision implements only the assigned Task 981 scope and binds the intended test-heavy workload. The executing Agent remains responsible for current ordinary authorization; the local guard does not authenticate native approval or lifecycle.

assertions.requirement: R1: Trashing a parent keeps its active child, grandchild, and contained sessions reachable
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested-folder trash/restore journey: create P > C > G and a session in C via authenticated APIs; trash P, reload the dashboard, and assert C and G are visible/navigable with the same session IDs and persisted parent relationships; restore P and assert its intended restoration behavior.

assertions.requirement: R2: Parent restoration does not overwrite a later explicit child move
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after trashing P and confirming C is promoted, explicitly move C to another existing folder through the folder API, restore P, and assert C remains at the explicit destination while deeper descendants and sessions remain intact.

assertions.requirement: R3: Permanent deletion and the shared expiry deletion operation promote surviving direct children safely
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — permanently delete a trashed P in P > C > G and assert C is promoted to P's former parent/root, G still points to C, and C's session IDs survive; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated database/storage case invokes the same folder deletion operation used by expiry, then asserts no child points at the removed P and deeper relationships and sessions are preserved.

assertions.requirement: R4: Lifecycle operations do not change another account's folder tree or sessions
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts and the isolated server deletion-path case — create a second account's folder/session tree as a control, run parent trash/permanent deletion or expiry for the first owner, then assert the control rows and relationships remain unchanged.

assertions.requirement: R5: Dashboard renders surviving nested descendants after parent removal
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after parent trash and after permanent deletion, reload the authenticated dashboard and assert child and grandchild folder headers and the contained session card are visible through ordinary navigation.

regression.rationale: This repairs existing persisted folder relationships and a visible dashboard failure; an active child can become unreachable and permanent deletion can leave it attached to a nonexistent parent.
regression.covers: Parent trash, restoration, explicit permanent deletion, and shared automatic-expiry deletion must preserve accessible descendants and sessions without changing another user's folder tree or overwriting an explicit later move.
regression.testLocation: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
regression.assertion: Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.

spec.regressionGuard:
**Covers:** Parent trash, restoration, explicit permanent deletion, and shared automatic-expiry deletion must preserve accessible descendants and sessions without changing another user's folder tree or overwriting an explicit later move.
**Test location:** tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
**What it checks:** Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.

spec.title: Preserve nested folder access
spec.scope:
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

# Preserve nested folder access

## Task identity
**Task ID:** c88fb94c-a4b5-4d2b-937c-65e1b99fa056
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** cc3b6bf33682701a17e89288bc1afe64d6440ac7856d0b5d6eb1ba5a2dfff15c

## Scope
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope
Do not recursively delete descendants or sessions, redesign folder navigation or permissions, change retention policy, broadly harden folder concurrency, add historical-data cleanup migrations, or change the policy for individually trashed sessions when their folder is restored first.

**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** This repairs existing persisted folder relationships and a visible dashboard failure; an active child can become unreachable and permanent deletion can leave it attached to a nonexistent parent.

spec.title: Preserve nested folder access
spec.scope:
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope
Do not recursively delete descendants or sessions, redesign folder navigation or permissions, change retention policy, broadly harden folder concurrency, add historical-data cleanup migrations, or change the policy for individually trashed sessions when their folder is restored first.
spec.why: The defect affects persisted parent relationships and rendered dashboard navigation; both the authenticated API lifecycle and actual browser visibility are needed alongside the scheduled lower-layer and compiler checks.

state.plan:
# Preserve nested folder access

## Task identity
**Task ID:** c88fb94c-a4b5-4d2b-937c-65e1b99fa056
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** cc3b6bf33682701a17e89288bc1afe64d6440ac7856d0b5d6eb1ba5a2dfff15c

## Scope
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope
Do not recursively delete descendants or sessions, redesign folder navigation or permissions, change retention policy, broadly harden folder concurrency, add historical-data cleanup migrations, or change the policy for individually trashed sessions when their folder is restored first.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** This repairs existing persisted folder relationships and a visible dashboard failure; an active child can become unreachable and permanent deletion can leave it attached to a nonexistent parent.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Assigned project Task 981 and its approved scope in the active task assignment.
**Owner direction:** Preserve access to surviving nested folders and sessions across parent trash, restore, permanent deletion, and automatic expiry, with cross-account isolation and actual dashboard coverage.
**Applicability:** This revision implements only the assigned Task 981 scope and binds the intended test-heavy workload. The executing Agent remains responsible for current ordinary authorization; the local guard does not authenticate native approval or lifecycle.

## Pre-existing failures to ignore
None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Flaky-test rule:** A passing retry establishes intermittency, not pre-existing provenance.

## Validation
**Command:** `test-heavy`
**Why:** The defect affects persisted parent relationships and rendered dashboard navigation; both the authenticated API lifecycle and actual browser visibility are needed alongside the scheduled lower-layer and compiler checks.
**Coverage evidence:** docs/validation/manifest.json; docs/validation/manifest.json test-heavy: typecheck checks TypeScript changes; unit-tests executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts for isolated shared expiry-deletion storage/API behavior; browser-tests runs scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs, which provisions and removes a disposable database and executes tests/folder-expand.spec.ts against authenticated folder APIs and dashboard visibility. The tier is bounded at 900000 ms. The disposable-browser-database path is required; any unavailable prerequisite blocks rather than permitting a weaker tier.; supported invocation: TASK_ID=c88fb94c-a4b5-4d2b-937c-65e1b99fa056 TASK_PLAN_FILE=.local/tasks/c88fb94c-a4b5-4d2b-937c-65e1b99fa056.md npm run gate:run -- --id c88fb94c-a4b5-4d2b-937c-65e1b99fa056 --tier test-heavy
**Do not switch tiers:** This task ID is strictly bound to this tier. Other tiers will block execution; changes require a supported amendment.

## Planned guard assertions
- R1: Trashing a parent keeps its active child, grandchild, and contained sessions reachable — tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested-folder trash/restore journey: create P > C > G and a session in C via authenticated APIs; trash P, reload the dashboard, and assert C and G are visible/navigable with the same session IDs and persisted parent relationships; restore P and assert its intended restoration behavior.
- R2: Parent restoration does not overwrite a later explicit child move — tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after trashing P and confirming C is promoted, explicitly move C to another existing folder through the folder API, restore P, and assert C remains at the explicit destination while deeper descendants and sessions remain intact.
- R3: Permanent deletion and the shared expiry deletion operation promote surviving direct children safely — tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — permanently delete a trashed P in P > C > G and assert C is promoted to P's former parent/root, G still points to C, and C's session IDs survive; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated database/storage case invokes the same folder deletion operation used by expiry, then asserts no child points at the removed P and deeper relationships and sessions are preserved.
- R4: Lifecycle operations do not change another account's folder tree or sessions — tests/folder-expand.spec.ts and the isolated server deletion-path case — create a second account's folder/session tree as a control, run parent trash/permanent deletion or expiry for the first owner, then assert the control rows and relationships remain unchanged.
- R5: Dashboard renders surviving nested descendants after parent removal — tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after parent trash and after permanent deletion, reload the authenticated dashboard and assert child and grandchild folder headers and the contained session card are visible through ordinary navigation.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** Parent trash, restoration, explicit permanent deletion, and shared automatic-expiry deletion must preserve accessible descendants and sessions without changing another user's folder tree or overwriting an explicit later move.
**Test location:** tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
**What it checks:** Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.

spec.title: Preserve nested folder access
spec.scope:
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope
Do not recursively delete descendants or sessions, redesign folder navigation or permissions, change retention policy, broadly harden folder concurrency, add historical-data cleanup migrations, or change the policy for individually trashed sessions when their folder is restored first.
spec.why: The defect affects persisted parent relationships and rendered dashboard navigation; both the authenticated API lifecycle and actual browser visibility are needed alongside the scheduled lower-layer and compiler checks.
spec.coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json test-heavy: typecheck checks TypeScript changes; unit-tests executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts for isolated shared expiry-deletion storage/API behavior; browser-tests runs scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs, which provisions and removes a disposable database and executes tests/folder-expand.spec.ts against authenticated folder APIs and dashboard visibility. The tier is bounded at 900000 ms. The disposable-browser-database path is required; any unavailable prerequisite blocks rather than permitting a weaker tier.

approval.reference: Assigned project Task 981 and its approved scope in the active task assignment.

state.plan:
# Preserve nested folder access

## Task identity
**Task ID:** c88fb94c-a4b5-4d2b-937c-65e1b99fa056
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** cc3b6bf33682701a17e89288bc1afe64d6440ac7856d0b5d6eb1ba5a2dfff15c

## Scope
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope
Do not recursively delete descendants or sessions, redesign folder navigation or permissions, change retention policy, broadly harden folder concurrency, add historical-data cleanup migrations, or change the policy for individually trashed sessions when their folder is restored first.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** This repairs existing persisted folder relationships and a visible dashboard failure; an active child can become unreachable and permanent deletion can leave it attached to a nonexistent parent.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Assigned project Task 981 and its approved scope in the active task assignment.
**Owner direction:** Preserve access to surviving nested folders and sessions across parent trash, restore, permanent deletion, and automatic expiry, with cross-account isolation and actual dashboard coverage.
**Applicability:** This revision implements only the assigned Task 981 scope and binds the intended test-heavy workload. The executing Agent remains responsible for current ordinary authorization; the local guard does not authenticate native approval or lifecycle.

## Pre-existing failures to ignore
None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Flaky-test rule:** A passing retry establishes intermittency, not pre-existing provenance.

## Validation
**Command:** `test-heavy`
**Why:** The defect affects persisted parent relationships and rendered dashboard navigation; both the authenticated API lifecycle and actual browser visibility are needed alongside the scheduled lower-layer and compiler checks.
**Coverage evidence:** docs/validation/manifest.json; docs/validation/manifest.json test-heavy: typecheck checks TypeScript changes; unit-tests executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts for isolated shared expiry-deletion storage/API behavior; browser-tests runs scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs, which provisions and removes a disposable database and executes tests/folder-expand.spec.ts against authenticated folder APIs and dashboard visibility. The tier is bounded at 900000 ms. The disposable-browser-database path is required; any unavailable prerequisite blocks rather than permitting a weaker tier.; supported invocation: TASK_ID=c88fb94c-a4b5-4d2b-937c-65e1b99fa056 TASK_PLAN_FILE=.local/tasks/c88fb94c-a4b5-4d2b-937c-65e1b99fa056.md npm run gate:run -- --id c88fb94c-a4b5-4d2b-937c-65e1b99fa056 --tier test-heavy
**Do not switch tiers:** This task ID is strictly bound to this tier. Other tiers will block execution; changes require a supported amendment.

## Planned guard assertions
- R1: Trashing a parent keeps its active child, grandchild, and contained sessions reachable — tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested-folder trash/restore journey: create P > C > G and a session in C via authenticated APIs; trash P, reload the dashboard, and assert C and G are visible/navigable with the same session IDs and persisted parent relationships; restore P and assert its intended restoration behavior.
- R2: Parent restoration does not overwrite a later explicit child move — tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after trashing P and confirming C is promoted, explicitly move C to another existing folder through the folder API, restore P, and assert C remains at the explicit destination while deeper descendants and sessions remain intact.
- R3: Permanent deletion and the shared expiry deletion operation promote surviving direct children safely — tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — permanently delete a trashed P in P > C > G and assert C is promoted to P's former parent/root, G still points to C, and C's session IDs survive; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated database/storage case invokes the same folder deletion operation used by expiry, then asserts no child points at the removed P and deeper relationships and sessions are preserved.
- R4: Lifecycle operations do not change another account's folder tree or sessions — tests/folder-expand.spec.ts and the isolated server deletion-path case — create a second account's folder/session tree as a control, run parent trash/permanent deletion or expiry for the first owner, then assert the control rows and relationships remain unchanged.
- R5: Dashboard renders surviving nested descendants after parent removal — tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after parent trash and after permanent deletion, reload the authenticated dashboard and assert child and grandchild folder headers and the contained session card are visible through ordinary navigation.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** Parent trash, restoration, explicit permanent deletion, and shared automatic-expiry deletion must preserve accessible descendants and sessions without changing another user's folder tree or overwriting an explicit later move.
**Test location:** tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
**What it checks:** Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.

spec.title: Preserve nested folder access
spec.scope:
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope
Do not recursively delete descendants or sessions, redesign folder navigation or permissions, change retention policy, broadly harden folder concurrency, add historical-data cleanup migrations, or change the policy for individually trashed sessions when their folder is restored first.
spec.why: The defect affects persisted parent relationships and rendered dashboard navigation; both the authenticated API lifecycle and actual browser visibility are needed alongside the scheduled lower-layer and compiler checks.
spec.coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json test-heavy: typecheck checks TypeScript changes; unit-tests executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts for isolated shared expiry-deletion storage/API behavior; browser-tests runs scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs, which provisions and removes a disposable database and executes tests/folder-expand.spec.ts against authenticated folder APIs and dashboard visibility. The tier is bounded at 900000 ms. The disposable-browser-database path is required; any unavailable prerequisite blocks rather than permitting a weaker tier.

approval.reference: Assigned project Task 981 and its approved scope in the active task assignment.
approval.direction: Preserve access to surviving nested folders and sessions across parent trash, restore, permanent deletion, and automatic expiry, with cross-account isolation and actual dashboard coverage.
approval.applicability: This revision implements only the assigned Task 981 scope and binds the intended test-heavy workload. The executing Agent remains responsible for current ordinary authorization; the local guard does not authenticate native approval or lifecycle.

assertions.requirement: R1: Trashing a parent keeps its active child, grandchild, and contained sessions reachable
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested-folder trash/restore journey: create P > C > G and a session in C via authenticated APIs; trash P, reload the dashboard, and assert C and G are visible/navigable with the same session IDs and persisted parent relationships; restore P and assert its intended restoration behavior.

assertions.requirement: R2: Parent restoration does not overwrite a later explicit child move
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after trashing P and confirming C is promoted, explicitly move C to another existing folder through the folder API, restore P, and assert C remains at the explicit destination while deeper descendants and sessions remain intact.

assertions.requirement: R3: Permanent deletion and the shared expiry deletion operation promote surviving direct children safely
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — permanently delete a trashed P in P > C > G and assert C is promoted to P's former parent/root, G still points to C, and C's session IDs survive; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated database/storage case invokes the same folder deletion operation used by expiry, then asserts no child points at the removed P and deeper relationships and sessions are preserved.

assertions.requirement: R4: Lifecycle operations do not change another account's folder tree or sessions
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts and the isolated server deletion-path case — create a second account's folder/session tree as a control, run parent trash/permanent deletion or expiry for the first owner, then assert the control rows and relationships remain unchanged.

assertions.requirement: R5: Dashboard renders surviving nested descendants after parent removal
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after parent trash and after permanent deletion, reload the authenticated dashboard and assert child and grandchild folder headers and the contained session card are visible through ordinary navigation.

regression.rationale: This repairs existing persisted folder relationships and a visible dashboard failure; an active child can become unreachable and permanent deletion can leave it attached to a nonexistent parent.
regression.covers: Parent trash, restoration, explicit permanent deletion, and shared automatic-expiry deletion must preserve accessible descendants and sessions without changing another user's folder tree or overwriting an explicit later move.
regression.testLocation: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
regression.assertion: Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.

spec.regressionGuard:

**Test location:** tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
**What it checks:** Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.

spec.title: Preserve nested folder access
spec.scope:
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope
Do not recursively delete descendants or sessions, redesign folder navigation or permissions, change retention policy, broadly harden folder concurrency, add historical-data cleanup migrations, or change the policy for individually trashed sessions when their folder is restored first.
spec.why: The defect affects persisted parent relationships and rendered dashboard navigation; both the authenticated API lifecycle and actual browser visibility are needed alongside the scheduled lower-layer and compiler checks.
spec.coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json test-heavy: typecheck checks TypeScript changes; unit-tests executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts for isolated shared expiry-deletion storage/API behavior; browser-tests runs scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs, which provisions and removes a disposable database and executes tests/folder-expand.spec.ts against authenticated folder APIs and dashboard visibility. The tier is bounded at 900000 ms. The disposable-browser-database path is required; any unavailable prerequisite blocks rather than permitting a weaker tier.

approval.reference: Assigned project Task 981 and its approved scope in the active task assignment.
approval.direction: Preserve access to surviving nested folders and sessions across parent trash, restore, permanent deletion, and automatic expiry, with cross-account isolation and actual dashboard coverage.
approval.applicability: This revision implements only the assigned Task 981 scope and binds the intended test-heavy workload. The executing Agent remains responsible for current ordinary authorization; the local guard does not authenticate native approval or lifecycle.

assertions.requirement: R1: Trashing a parent keeps its active child, grandchild, and contained sessions reachable
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested-folder trash/restore journey: create P > C > G and a session in C via authenticated APIs; trash P, reload the dashboard, and assert C and G are visible/navigable with the same session IDs and persisted parent relationships; restore P and assert its intended restoration behavior.

assertions.requirement: R2: Parent restoration does not overwrite a later explicit child move
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after trashing P and confirming C is promoted, explicitly move C to another existing folder through the folder API, restore P, and assert C remains at the explicit destination while deeper descendants and sessions remain intact.

assertions.requirement: R3: Permanent deletion and the shared expiry deletion operation promote surviving direct children safely
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — permanently delete a trashed P in P > C > G and assert C is promoted to P's former parent/root, G still points to C, and C's session IDs survive; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated database/storage case invokes the same folder deletion operation used by expiry, then asserts no child points at the removed P and deeper relationships and sessions are preserved.

assertions.requirement: R4: Lifecycle operations do not change another account's folder tree or sessions
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts and the isolated server deletion-path case — create a second account's folder/session tree as a control, run parent trash/permanent deletion or expiry for the first owner, then assert the control rows and relationships remain unchanged.

assertions.requirement: R5: Dashboard renders surviving nested descendants after parent removal
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after parent trash and after permanent deletion, reload the authenticated dashboard and assert child and grandchild folder headers and the contained session card are visible through ordinary navigation.

regression.rationale: This repairs existing persisted folder relationships and a visible dashboard failure; an active child can become unreachable and permanent deletion can leave it attached to a nonexistent parent.
regression.covers: Parent trash, restoration, explicit permanent deletion, and shared automatic-expiry deletion must preserve accessible descendants and sessions without changing another user's folder tree or overwriting an explicit later move.
regression.testLocation: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
regression.assertion: Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.

spec.regressionGuard:
**Covers:** Parent trash, restoration, explicit permanent deletion, and shared automatic-expiry deletion must preserve accessible descendants and sessions without changing another user's folder tree or overwriting an explicit later move.
**Test location:** tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
**What it checks:** Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.

spec.title: Preserve nested folder access
spec.scope:
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope

# Preserve nested folder access

## Task identity
**Task ID:** c88fb94c-a4b5-4d2b-937c-65e1b99fa056
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** cc3b6bf33682701a17e89288bc1afe64d6440ac7856d0b5d6eb1ba5a2dfff15c

## Scope
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope
Do not recursively delete descendants or sessions, redesign folder navigation or permissions, change retention policy, broadly harden folder concurrency, add historical-data cleanup migrations, or change the policy for individually trashed sessions when their folder is restored first.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** This repairs existing persisted folder relationships and a visible dashboard failure; an active child can become unreachable and permanent deletion can leave it attached to a nonexistent parent.

spec.title: Preserve nested folder access
spec.scope:
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope
Do not recursively delete descendants or sessions, redesign folder navigation or permissions, change retention policy, broadly harden folder concurrency, add historical-data cleanup migrations, or change the policy for individually trashed sessions when their folder is restored first.
spec.why: The defect affects persisted parent relationships and rendered dashboard navigation; both the authenticated API lifecycle and actual browser visibility are needed alongside the scheduled lower-layer and compiler checks.
spec.coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json test-heavy: typecheck checks TypeScript changes; unit-tests executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts for isolated shared expiry-deletion storage/API behavior; browser-tests runs scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs, which provisions and removes a disposable database and executes tests/folder-expand.spec.ts against authenticated folder APIs and dashboard visibility. The tier is bounded at 900000 ms. The disposable-browser-database path is required; any unavailable prerequisite blocks rather than permitting a weaker tier.

approval.reference: Assigned project Task 981 and its approved scope in the active task assignment.
approval.direction: Preserve access to surviving nested folders and sessions across parent trash, restore, permanent deletion, and automatic expiry, with cross-account isolation and actual dashboard coverage.
approval.applicability: This revision implements only the assigned Task 981 scope and binds the intended test-heavy workload. The executing Agent remains responsible for current ordinary authorization; the local guard does not authenticate native approval or lifecycle.

assertions.requirement: R1: Trashing a parent keeps its active child, grandchild, and contained sessions reachable
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested-folder trash/restore journey: create P > C > G and a session in C via authenticated APIs; trash P, reload the dashboard, and assert C and G are visible/navigable with the same session IDs and persisted parent relationships; restore P and assert its intended restoration behavior.

assertions.requirement: R2: Parent restoration does not overwrite a later explicit child move
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after trashing P and confirming C is promoted, explicitly move C to another existing folder through the folder API, restore P, and assert C remains at the explicit destination while deeper descendants and sessions remain intact.

assertions.requirement: R3: Permanent deletion and the shared expiry deletion operation promote surviving direct children safely
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — permanently delete a trashed P in P > C > G and assert C is promoted to P's former parent/root, G still points to C, and C's session IDs survive; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated database/storage case invokes the same folder deletion operation used by expiry, then asserts no child points at the removed P and deeper relationships and sessions are preserved.

assertions.requirement: R4: Lifecycle operations do not change another account's folder tree or sessions
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts and the isolated server deletion-path case — create a second account's folder/session tree as a control, run parent trash/permanent deletion or expiry for the first owner, then assert the control rows and relationships remain unchanged.

assertions.requirement: R5: Dashboard renders surviving nested descendants after parent removal
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after parent trash and after permanent deletion, reload the authenticated dashboard and assert child and grandchild folder headers and the contained session card are visible through ordinary navigation.

regression.rationale: This repairs existing persisted folder relationships and a visible dashboard failure; an active child can become unreachable and permanent deletion can leave it attached to a nonexistent parent.
regression.covers: Parent trash, restoration, explicit permanent deletion, and shared automatic-expiry deletion must preserve accessible descendants and sessions without changing another user's folder tree or overwriting an explicit later move.
regression.testLocation: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
regression.assertion: Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.

spec.regressionGuard:
**Covers:** Parent trash, restoration, explicit permanent deletion, and shared automatic-expiry deletion must preserve accessible descendants and sessions without changing another user's folder tree or overwriting an explicit later move.
**Test location:** tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
**What it checks:** Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.

spec.title: Preserve nested folder access
spec.scope:
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope
Do not recursively delete descendants or sessions, redesign folder navigation or permissions, change retention policy, broadly harden folder concurrency, add historical-data cleanup migrations, or change the policy for individually trashed sessions when their folder is restored first.
spec.why: The defect affects persisted parent relationships and rendered dashboard navigation; both the authenticated API lifecycle and actual browser visibility are needed alongside the scheduled lower-layer and compiler checks.
spec.coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json test-heavy: typecheck checks TypeScript changes; unit-tests executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts for isolated shared expiry-deletion storage/API behavior; browser-tests runs scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs, which provisions and removes a disposable database and executes tests/folder-expand.spec.ts against authenticated folder APIs and dashboard visibility. The tier is bounded at 900000 ms. The disposable-browser-database path is required; any unavailable prerequisite blocks rather than permitting a weaker tier.

approval.direction: Preserve access to surviving nested folders and sessions across parent trash, restore, permanent deletion, and automatic expiry, with cross-account isolation and actual dashboard coverage.
approval.applicability: This revision implements only the assigned Task 981 scope and binds the intended test-heavy workload. The executing Agent remains responsible for current ordinary authorization; the local guard does not authenticate native approval or lifecycle.

assertions.requirement: R1: Trashing a parent keeps its active child, grandchild, and contained sessions reachable
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested-folder trash/restore journey: create P > C > G and a session in C via authenticated APIs; trash P, reload the dashboard, and assert C and G are visible/navigable with the same session IDs and persisted parent relationships; restore P and assert its intended restoration behavior.

assertions.requirement: R2: Parent restoration does not overwrite a later explicit child move
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after trashing P and confirming C is promoted, explicitly move C to another existing folder through the folder API, restore P, and assert C remains at the explicit destination while deeper descendants and sessions remain intact.

assertions.requirement: R3: Permanent deletion and the shared expiry deletion operation promote surviving direct children safely
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — permanently delete a trashed P in P > C > G and assert C is promoted to P's former parent/root, G still points to C, and C's session IDs survive; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated database/storage case invokes the same folder deletion operation used by expiry, then asserts no child points at the removed P and deeper relationships and sessions are preserved.

regression.testLocation: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
regression.assertion: Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.

spec.title: Preserve nested folder access
spec.scope:
Repair folder lifecycle behavior that hides active descendants when a parent is trashed and leaves surviving descendants with a missing parent after permanent deletion or automatic expiry. Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. Restoring the parent must remain possible and must not silently override later explicit moves.

## Out of scope
Do not recursively delete descendants or sessions, redesign folder navigation or permissions, change retention policy, broadly harden folder concurrency, add historical-data cleanup migrations, or change the policy for individually trashed sessions when their folder is restored first.
spec.why: The defect affects persisted parent relationships and rendered dashboard navigation; both the authenticated API lifecycle and actual browser visibility are needed alongside the scheduled lower-layer and compiler checks.
spec.coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json test-heavy: typecheck checks TypeScript changes; unit-tests executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts for isolated shared expiry-deletion storage/API behavior; browser-tests runs scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs, which provisions and removes a disposable database and executes tests/folder-expand.spec.ts against authenticated folder APIs and dashboard visibility. The tier is bounded at 900000 ms. The disposable-browser-database path is required; any unavailable prerequisite blocks rather than permitting a weaker tier.

approval.reference: Assigned project Task 981 and its approved scope in the active task assignment.
approval.direction: Preserve access to surviving nested folders and sessions across parent trash, restore, permanent deletion, and automatic expiry, with cross-account isolation and actual dashboard coverage.
approval.applicability: This revision implements only the assigned Task 981 scope and binds the intended test-heavy workload. The executing Agent remains responsible for current ordinary authorization; the local guard does not authenticate native approval or lifecycle.

assertions.requirement: R1: Trashing a parent keeps its active child, grandchild, and contained sessions reachable
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested-folder trash/restore journey: create P > C > G and a session in C via authenticated APIs; trash P, reload the dashboard, and assert C and G are visible/navigable with the same session IDs and persisted parent relationships; restore P and assert its intended restoration behavior.

assertions.requirement: R2: Parent restoration does not overwrite a later explicit child move
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after trashing P and confirming C is promoted, explicitly move C to another existing folder through the folder API, restore P, and assert C remains at the explicit destination while deeper descendants and sessions remain intact.

assertions.requirement: R3: Permanent deletion and the shared expiry deletion operation promote surviving direct children safely
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — permanently delete a trashed P in P > C > G and assert C is promoted to P's former parent/root, G still points to C, and C's session IDs survive; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated database/storage case invokes the same folder deletion operation used by expiry, then asserts no child points at the removed P and deeper relationships and sessions are preserved.

assertions.requirement: R4: Lifecycle operations do not change another account's folder tree or sessions
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts and the isolated server deletion-path case — create a second account's folder/session tree as a control, run parent trash/permanent deletion or expiry for the first owner, then assert the control rows and relationships remain unchanged.

assertions.requirement: R5: Dashboard renders surviving nested descendants after parent removal
assertions.check: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — after parent trash and after permanent deletion, reload the authenticated dashboard and assert child and grandchild folder headers and the contained session card are visible through ordinary navigation.

regression.rationale: This repairs existing persisted folder relationships and a visible dashboard failure; an active child can become unreachable and permanent deletion can leave it attached to a nonexistent parent.
regression.covers: Parent trash, restoration, explicit permanent deletion, and shared automatic-expiry deletion must preserve accessible descendants and sessions without changing another user's folder tree or overwriting an explicit later move.
regression.testLocation: tests/folder-expand.spec.ts — nested parent trash/restore, explicit child move, permanent deletion, and dashboard visibility; server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — isolated shared expiry-deletion operation.
regression.assertion: Using authenticated folder APIs, build P > C > G with a session in C and a second-account control tree; after each lifecycle path assert the child is promoted only as needed, G remains attached to C, session IDs survive, parent pointers never target the deleted folder, the dashboard shows C/G/session after reload, explicit later moves survive restore, and control-account rows remain unchanged.

spec.title: Preserve nested folder access

Promote only direct children to the trashed folder's surviving parent (or root), preserve deeper descendant relationships and all sessions, and scope changes to the folder owner. ## Out of scope

# Enforce photo-management capability for photo duplication

## Task identity
**Task ID:** 5b7b81f0-7985-48a0-be6f-cf8ea1f13322
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** 1c473ac807c45b104d7ca36fd94163ae3d0d4d4e97dbb5dd71bc8a81b98a6736

## Scope
Fix the account capability middleware in server/routes.ts so only session duplication selects session_create and photo duplication selects photo_management. Preserve session access, edit and lock checks. Add HTTP middleware regression coverage for all four combinations of session_create and photo_management, checking denial payloads and that denied requests cannot reach mutation handlers. No new features or unrelated authorization changes.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true

## Approval evidence

**Owner direction:** Fix the photo duplication authorization bypass without introducing features
**Applicability:** Narrow server middleware repair and regression coverage within the assigned scope

# Enforce photo-management capability for photo duplication

## Task identity
**Task ID:** 5b7b81f0-7985-48a0-be6f-cf8ea1f13322
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** 1c473ac807c45b104d7ca36fd94163ae3d0d4d4e97dbb5dd71bc8a81b98a6736

## Scope
Fix the account capability middleware in server/routes.ts so only session duplication selects session_create and photo duplication selects photo_management. Preserve session access, edit and lock checks. Add HTTP middleware regression coverage for all four combinations of session_create and photo_management, checking denial payloads and that denied requests cannot reach mutation handlers. No new features or unrelated authorization changes.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** Repairs a server-side authorization bypass permitting unauthorized photo writes.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Assigned task 1010 in the active conversation
**Owner direction:** Fix the photo duplication authorization bypass without introducing features
**Applicability:** Narrow server middleware repair and regression coverage within the assigned scope

## Pre-existing failures to ignore
None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Flaky-test rule:** A passing retry establishes intermittency, not pre-existing provenance.

## Validation
**Command:** `test-standard`
**Why:** Backend authorization needs executable HTTP regression tests and compiler checks; the fast tier does not run route tests.
**Coverage evidence:** docs/validation/manifest.json; docs/validation/manifest.json test-standard includes typecheck and unit-tests; npm run test:unit executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts.; supported invocation: TASK_ID=5b7b81f0-7985-48a0-be6f-cf8ea1f13322 TASK_PLAN_FILE=.local/tasks/5b7b81f0-7985-48a0-be6f-cf8ea1f13322.md npm run gate:run -- --id 5b7b81f0-7985-48a0-be6f-cf8ea1f13322 --tier test-standard
**Do not switch tiers:** This task ID is strictly bound to this tier. Other tiers will block execution; changes require a supported amendment.

## Planned guard assertions
- R1 photo duplication — With session_create true and photo_management false, POST photo duplication returns 403 capability_denied for photo_management without running its mutation handler; all four capability combinations follow photo_management only.
- R2 session duplication — POST session creation and duplication remain governed by session_create only across all four capability combinations, independently of photo_management.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** Approved users with edit access and session creation enabled must not bypass a disabled photo-management capability by calling photo duplication.
**Test location:** server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — account capability route guard, duplication capability matrix
**What it checks:** Real HTTP requests through the production middleware return exact 403 photo_management denials before mutation handlers run; permitted photo duplication and session operations follow their own capabilities across all four combinations.

- R2 session duplication — POST session creation and duplication remain governed by session_create only across all four capability combinations, independently of photo_management.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** Approved users with edit access and session creation enabled must not bypass a disabled photo-management capability by calling photo duplication.
**Test location:** server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — account capability route guard, duplication capability matrix
**What it checks:** Real HTTP requests through the production middleware return exact 403 photo_management denials before mutation handlers run; permitted photo duplication and session operations follow their own capabilities across all four combinations.

state.plan:
# Enforce photo-management capability for photo duplication

## Task identity
**Task ID:** 5b7b81f0-7985-48a0-be6f-cf8ea1f13322
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** 1c473ac807c45b104d7ca36fd94163ae3d0d4d4e97dbb5dd71bc8a81b98a6736

## Scope
Fix the account capability middleware in server/routes.ts so only session duplication selects session_create and photo duplication selects photo_management. Preserve session access, edit and lock checks. Add HTTP middleware regression coverage for all four combinations of session_create and photo_management, checking denial payloads and that denied requests cannot reach mutation handlers. No new features or unrelated authorization changes.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** Repairs a server-side authorization bypass permitting unauthorized photo writes.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Assigned task 1010 in the active conversation
**Owner direction:** Fix the photo duplication authorization bypass without introducing features
**Applicability:** Narrow server middleware repair and regression coverage within the assigned scope

## Pre-existing failures to ignore
None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Flaky-test rule:** A passing retry establishes intermittency, not pre-existing provenance.

## Validation
**Command:** `test-standard`
**Why:** Backend authorization needs executable HTTP regression tests and compiler checks; the fast tier does not run route tests.
**Coverage evidence:** docs/validation/manifest.json; docs/validation/manifest.json test-standard includes typecheck and unit-tests; npm run test:unit executes server/__tests__/routes.test.ts.; supported invocation: TASK_ID=5b7b81f0-7985-48a0-be6f-cf8ea1f13322 TASK_PLAN_FILE=.local/tasks/5b7b81f0-7985-48a0-be6f-cf8ea1f13322.md npm run gate:run -- --id 5b7b81f0-7985-48a0-be6f-cf8ea1f13322 --tier test-standard
**Do not switch tiers:** This task ID is strictly bound to this tier. Other tiers will block execution; changes require a supported amendment.

## Planned guard assertions
- R1 photo duplication — With session_create true and photo_management false, POST photo duplication returns 403 capability_denied for photo_management without running its mutation handler; all four capability combinations follow photo_management only.
- R2 session duplication — POST session creation and duplication remain governed by session_create only across all four capability combinations, independently of photo_management.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** Approved users with edit access and session creation enabled must not bypass a disabled photo-management capability by calling photo duplication.
**Test location:** server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — account capability route guard, duplication capability matrix
**What it checks:** Real HTTP requests through the production middleware return exact 403 photo_management denials before mutation handlers run; permitted photo duplication and session operations follow their own capabilities across all four combinations.

# Enforce photo-management capability for photo duplication

## Task identity
**Task ID:** 5b7b81f0-7985-48a0-be6f-cf8ea1f13322
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** 1c473ac807c45b104d7ca36fd94163ae3d0d4d4e97dbb5dd71bc8a81b98a6736

Fix the account capability middleware in server/routes.ts so only session duplication selects session_create and photo duplication selects photo_management. state.plan:
# Session Authorization Gaps

## Task identity
**Task ID:** f208beda-d34e-4b11-9c15-0342f3b9efe5
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** 1c473ac807c45b104d7ca36fd94163ae3d0d4d4e97dbb5dd71bc8a81b98a6736

## Scope
Harden existing session authorization only: exclude soft-deleted sessions from shared performance and role comparison aggregates, and require canEdit for review response and review cohort POSTs. Preserve live session aggregates, existing review reads, editor/owner writes, same-session entry validation, and nonmember/trashed-session denial. Add regression coverage to the existing registered routes tests.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** Repairs existing protected-data visibility and read-only role boundaries in session storage aggregates and review writes.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Assigned task 1013 in the active conversation
**Owner direction:** Fix the two session authorization vulnerabilities without adding features.
**Applicability:** This plan implements only the assigned aggregate scoping and review role enforcement fixes with recurrence tests.

## Pre-existing failures to ignore
None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Flaky-test rule:** A passing retry establishes intermittency, not pre-existing provenance.

## Validation
**Command:** `test-standard`
**Why:** Backend authorization changes require database-backed aggregate and production HTTP route tests as well as compiler and lint checks.
**Coverage evidence:** docs/validation/manifest.json; docs/validation/manifest.json test-standard unit-tests runs server/__tests__/routes.test.ts, covering both storage aggregates and production review POST handlers; typecheck checks application and test types.; supported invocation: TASK_ID=f208beda-d34e-4b11-9c15-0342f3b9efe5 TASK_PLAN_FILE=.local/tasks/f208beda-d34e-4b11-9c15-0342f3b9efe5.md npm run gate:run -- --id f208beda-d34e-4b11-9c15-0342f3b9efe5 --tier test-standard
**Do not switch tiers:** This task ID is strictly bound to this tier. Other tiers will block execution; changes require a supported amendment.

## Planned guard assertions
- Trashing a shared session withdraws its aggregate inventory and contributor visibility. — Database-backed calls to both real storage aggregate methods omit trashed sessions and their totals, preserve active ones, allow restoration, and exclude revoked memberships.
- Read-only users cannot persist review decisions or anchor review cohorts. — Real production HTTP POSTs deny viewers with 403 and no persisted mutation, allow editor and owner writes, and retain 404 access denial plus 400 wrong-session entry validation.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** A retained collaborator row must not expose trashed-session aggregate data; a viewer must not create or overwrite review responses or anchor a review cohort.
**Test location:** server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — session aggregate visibility and review write authorization cases
**What it checks:** Assert exact visible session IDs and role totals before trash, after trash, restore, and revocation; assert HTTP 403 and unchanged state for viewer POSTs, successful owner/editor POSTs, and preserved nonmember, trash, and wrong-session entry denial.

state.plan:
# Session Authorization Gaps

## Task identity
**Task ID:** f208beda-d34e-4b11-9c15-0342f3b9efe5
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** 1c473ac807c45b104d7ca36fd94163ae3d0d4d4e97dbb5dd71bc8a81b98a6736

## Scope
Harden existing session authorization only: exclude soft-deleted sessions from shared performance and role comparison aggregates, and require canEdit for review response and review cohort POSTs. Preserve live session aggregates, existing review reads, editor/owner writes, same-session entry validation, and nonmember/trashed-session denial. Add regression coverage to the existing registered routes tests.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** Repairs existing protected-data visibility and read-only role boundaries in session storage aggregates and review writes.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Assigned task 1013 in the active conversation
**Owner direction:** Fix the two session authorization vulnerabilities without adding features.
**Applicability:** This plan implements only the assigned aggregate scoping and review role enforcement fixes with recurrence tests.

## Pre-existing failures to ignore
None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Flaky-test rule:** A passing retry establishes intermittency, not pre-existing provenance.

## Validation
**Command:** `test-standard`
**Why:** Backend authorization changes require database-backed aggregate and production HTTP route tests as well as compiler and lint checks.
**Coverage evidence:** docs/validation/manifest.json; docs/validation/manifest.json test-standard unit-tests runs server/__tests__/routes.test.ts, covering both storage aggregates and production review POST handlers; typecheck checks application and test types.; supported invocation: TASK_ID=f208beda-d34e-4b11-9c15-0342f3b9efe5 TASK_PLAN_FILE=.local/tasks/f208beda-d34e-4b11-9c15-0342f3b9efe5.md npm run gate:run -- --id f208beda-d34e-4b11-9c15-0342f3b9efe5 --tier test-standard
**Do not switch tiers:** This task ID is strictly bound to this tier. Other tiers will block execution; changes require a supported amendment.

## Planned guard assertions
- Trashing a shared session withdraws its aggregate inventory and contributor visibility. — Database-backed calls to both real storage aggregate methods omit trashed sessions and their totals, preserve active ones, allow restoration, and exclude revoked memberships.
- Read-only users cannot persist review decisions or anchor review cohorts. — Real production HTTP POSTs deny viewers with 403 and no persisted mutation, allow editor and owner writes, and retain 404 access denial plus 400 wrong-session entry validation.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** A retained collaborator row must not expose trashed-session aggregate data; a viewer must not create or overwrite review responses or anchor a review cohort.
**Test location:** server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — session aggregate visibility and review write authorization cases
**What it checks:** Assert exact visible session IDs and role totals before trash, after trash, restore, and revocation; assert HTTP 403 and unchanged state for viewer POSTs, successful owner/editor POSTs, and preserved nonmember, trash, and wrong-session entry denial.

# Session Authorization Gaps

## Task identity
**Task ID:** f208beda-d34e-4b11-9c15-0342f3b9efe5
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** 1c473ac807c45b104d7ca36fd94163ae3d0d4d4e97dbb5dd71bc8a81b98a6736

## Scope
Harden existing session authorization only: exclude soft-deleted sessions from shared performance and role comparison aggregates, and require canEdit for review response and review cohort POSTs. Preserve live session aggregates, existing review reads, editor/owner writes, same-session entry validation, and nonmember/trashed-session denial. Add regression coverage to the existing registered routes tests.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** Repairs existing protected-data visibility and read-only role boundaries in session storage aggregates and review writes.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Assigned task 1013 in the active conversation
**Owner direction:** Fix the two session authorization vulnerabilities without adding features.
**Applicability:** This plan implements only the assigned aggregate scoping and review role enforcement fixes with recurrence tests.

## Pre-existing failures to ignore
None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Flaky-test rule:** A passing retry establishes intermittency, not pre-existing provenance.

## Validation
**Command:** `test-standard`
**Why:** Backend authorization changes require database-backed aggregate and production HTTP route tests as well as compiler and lint checks.
**Coverage evidence:** docs/validation/manifest.json; docs/validation/manifest.json test-standard unit-tests runs server/__tests__/routes.test.ts, covering both storage aggregates and production review POST handlers; typecheck checks application and test types.; supported invocation: TASK_ID=f208beda-d34e-4b11-9c15-0342f3b9efe5 TASK_PLAN_FILE=.local/tasks/f208beda-d34e-4b11-9c15-0342f3b9efe5.md npm run gate:run -- --id f208beda-d34e-4b11-9c15-0342f3b9efe5 --tier test-standard
**Do not switch tiers:** This task ID is strictly bound to this tier. Other tiers will block execution; changes require a supported amendment.

## Planned guard assertions
- Trashing a shared session withdraws its aggregate inventory and contributor visibility. — Database-backed calls to both real storage aggregate methods omit trashed sessions and their totals, preserve active ones, allow restoration, and exclude revoked memberships.
- Read-only users cannot persist review decisions or anchor review cohorts. — Real production HTTP POSTs deny viewers with 403 and no persisted mutation, allow editor and owner writes, and retain 404 access denial plus 400 wrong-session entry validation.

**Covers:** A retained collaborator row must not expose trashed-session aggregate data; a viewer must not create or overwrite review responses or anchor a review cohort.
**Test location:** server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — session aggregate visibility and review write authorization cases
**What it checks:** Assert exact visible session IDs and role totals before trash, after trash, restore, and revocation; assert HTTP 403 and unchanged state for viewer POSTs, successful owner/editor POSTs, and preserved nonmember, trash, and wrong-session entry denial.

state.plan:
# Session Authorization Gaps

## Task identity
**Task ID:** f208beda-d34e-4b11-9c15-0342f3b9efe5
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** 1c473ac807c45b104d7ca36fd94163ae3d0d4d4e97dbb5dd71bc8a81b98a6736

## Scope
Harden existing session authorization only: exclude soft-deleted sessions from shared performance and role comparison aggregates, and require canEdit for review response and review cohort POSTs. Preserve live session aggregates, existing review reads, editor/owner writes, same-session entry validation, and nonmember/trashed-session denial. Add regression coverage to the existing registered routes tests.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** Repairs existing protected-data visibility and read-only role boundaries in session storage aggregates and review writes.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Assigned task 1013 in the active conversation
**Owner direction:** Fix the two session authorization vulnerabilities without adding features.
**Applicability:** This plan implements only the assigned aggregate scoping and review role enforcement fixes with recurrence tests.

## Pre-existing failures to ignore
None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Flaky-test rule:** A passing retry establishes intermittency, not pre-existing provenance.

## Validation
**Command:** `test-standard`
**Why:** Backend authorization changes require database-backed aggregate and production HTTP route tests as well as compiler and lint checks.
**Coverage evidence:** docs/validation/manifest.json; docs/validation/manifest.json test-standard unit-tests runs server/__tests__/routes.test.ts, covering both storage aggregates and production review POST handlers; typecheck checks application and test types.; supported invocation: TASK_ID=f208beda-d34e-4b11-9c15-0342f3b9efe5 TASK_PLAN_FILE=.local/tasks/f208beda-d34e-4b11-9c15-0342f3b9efe5.md npm run gate:run -- --id f208beda-d34e-4b11-9c15-0342f3b9efe5 --tier test-standard
**Do not switch tiers:** This task ID is strictly bound to this tier. Other tiers will block execution; changes require a supported amendment.

## Planned guard assertions
- Trashing a shared session withdraws its aggregate inventory and contributor visibility. — Database-backed calls to both real storage aggregate methods omit trashed sessions and their totals, preserve active ones, allow restoration, and exclude revoked memberships.
- Read-only users cannot persist review decisions or anchor review cohorts. — Real production HTTP POSTs deny viewers with 403 and no persisted mutation, allow editor and owner writes, and retain 404 access denial plus 400 wrong-session entry validation.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** A retained collaborator row must not expose trashed-session aggregate data; a viewer must not create or overwrite review responses or anchor a review cohort.
**Test location:** server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — session aggregate visibility and review write authorization cases
**What it checks:** Assert exact visible session IDs and role totals before trash, after trash, restore, and revocation; assert HTTP 403 and unchanged state for viewer POSTs, successful owner/editor POSTs, and preserved nonmember, trash, and wrong-session entry denial.

state.plan:
# Enforce label scan pin, photo and session ownership

## Task identity
**Task ID:** aa4227c8-a7e9-4c86-a6e6-982fed1ec67c
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** 1c473ac807c45b104d7ca36fd94163ae3d0d4d4e97dbb5dd71bc8a81b98a6736

## Scope
Repair the assigned label scan BOLA in both production analyze-labels routes and upsertScanResults. Reject missing, malformed or mismatched pin/photo/session identifiers before image/provider work; protect persistence against mismatched ownership and foreign conflict rows, atomically. Preserve valid scanning, collaborator access, provider and UI flows. No schema changes.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** Fixes a persistent cross-session data-integrity and object-authorization vulnerability.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Assigned task 1012 in the active conversation
**Owner direction:** Patch cross-session label scan result overwrites without new product flows
**Applicability:** Route and persistence security hardening and regression coverage are within assigned scope; independent verification not selected

## Pre-existing failures to ignore
None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Flaky-test rule:** A passing retry establishes intermittency, not pre-existing provenance.

## Validation
**Command:** `test-standard`
**Why:** The backend authorization repair needs compiler checks, executable production-route regressions and real PostgreSQL persistence coverage.
**Coverage evidence:** docs/validation/manifest.json; docs/validation/manifest.json test-standard typecheck and unit-tests include server/__tests__/routes.test.ts, where HTTP and isolated PostgreSQL regression cases run.; supported invocation: TASK_ID=aa4227c8-a7e9-4c86-a6e6-982fed1ec67c TASK_PLAN_FILE=.local/tasks/aa4227c8-a7e9-4c86-a6e6-982fed1ec67c.md npm run gate:run -- --id aa4227c8-a7e9-4c86-a6e6-982fed1ec67c --tier test-standard
**Do not switch tiers:** This task ID is strictly bound to this tier. Other tiers will block execution; changes require a supported amendment.

## Planned guard assertions
- R1 request ownership — Both production routes reject forged foreign, wrong-photo, missing and malformed pin IDs before provider work and leave victim results unchanged.
- R2 persistence isolation — The production storage method rejects mismatched pin/photo/session relationships and foreign conflict rows without changing any rows in a mixed batch.
- R3 valid scans — Valid same-scope inserts and updates succeed; valid editor access remains accepted.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** R1 client-controlled pin IDs in both endpoints; R2 database insert and conflict update isolation plus atomic batch rollback; R3 authorized scanning compatibility
**Test location:** server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — label scan object authorization HTTP and PostgreSQL cases
**What it checks:** Send forged pin IDs through actual production routes and assert rejection and unchanged victim data; call actual storage with invalid ownership and foreign conflicts and assert rejection plus batch rollback; assert normal inserts and updates succeed.

# Enforce label scan pin, photo and session ownership

## Task identity
**Task ID:** aa4227c8-a7e9-4c86-a6e6-982fed1ec67c
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** 1c473ac807c45b104d7ca36fd94163ae3d0d4d4e97dbb5dd71bc8a81b98a6736

## Scope
Repair the assigned label scan BOLA in both production analyze-labels routes and upsertScanResults. Reject missing, malformed or mismatched pin/photo/session identifiers before image/provider work; protect persistence against mismatched ownership and foreign conflict rows, atomically. Preserve valid scanning, collaborator access, provider and UI flows. No schema changes.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** Fixes a persistent cross-session data-integrity and object-authorization vulnerability.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Assigned task 1012 in the active conversation
**Owner direction:** Patch cross-session label scan result overwrites without new product flows
**Applicability:** Route and persistence security hardening and regression coverage are within assigned scope; independent verification not selected
