None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Why:** The backend authorization repair needs compiler checks, executable production-route regressions and real PostgreSQL persistence coverage.

- R2 persistence isolation — The production storage method rejects mismatched pin/photo/session relationships and foreign conflict rows without changing any rows in a mixed batch.
- R3 valid scans — Valid same-scope inserts and updates succeed; valid editor access remains accepted.

spec.title: Enforce label scan pin, photo and session ownership
spec.scope: Repair the assigned label scan BOLA in both production analyze-labels routes and upsertScanResults. Reject missing, malformed or mismatched pin/photo/session identifiers before image/provider work; protect persistence against mismatched ownership and foreign conflict rows, atomically. Preserve valid scanning, collaborator access, provider and UI flows. No schema changes.
spec.why: The backend authorization repair needs compiler checks, executable production-route regressions and real PostgreSQL persistence coverage.
spec.coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json test-standard typecheck and unit-tests include server/__tests__/routes.test.ts, where HTTP and isolated PostgreSQL regression cases run.

approval.direction: Patch cross-session label scan result overwrites without new product flows
approval.applicability: Route and persistence security hardening and regression coverage are within assigned scope; independent verification not selected

assertions.requirement: R1 request ownership
assertions.check: Both production routes reject forged foreign, wrong-photo, missing and malformed pin IDs before provider work and leave victim results unchanged.

assertions.requirement: R2 persistence isolation
assertions.check: The production storage method rejects mismatched pin/photo/session relationships and foreign conflict rows without changing any rows in a mixed batch.

assertions.requirement: R3 valid scans

state.plan:
# Enforce label scan pin, photo and session ownership

## Task identity
**Task ID:** aa4227c8-a7e9-4c86-a6e6-982fed1ec67c
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** 1c473ac807c45b104d7ca36fd94163ae3d0d4d4e97dbb5dd71bc8a81b98a6736

## Scope
Repair the assigned label scan BOLA in both production analyze-labels routes and upsertScanResults. Reject missing, malformed or mismatched pin/photo/session identifiers before image/provider work; protect persistence against mismatched ownership and foreign conflict rows, atomically. Preserve valid scanning, collaborator access, provider and UI flows. No schema changes.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** Fixes a persistent cross-session data-integrity and object-authorization vulnerability.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Assigned task 1012 in the active conversation
**Owner direction:** Patch cross-session label scan result overwrites without new product flows
**Applicability:** Route and persistence security hardening and regression coverage are within assigned scope; independent verification not selected

## Pre-existing failures to ignore
None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Flaky-test rule:** A passing retry establishes intermittency, not pre-existing provenance.

## Validation
**Command:** `test-standard`
**Why:** The backend authorization repair needs compiler checks, executable production-route regressions and real PostgreSQL persistence coverage.
**Coverage evidence:** docs/validation/manifest.json; docs/validation/manifest.json test-standard typecheck and unit-tests include server/__tests__/routes.test.ts, where HTTP and isolated PostgreSQL regression cases run.; supported invocation: TASK_ID=aa4227c8-a7e9-4c86-a6e6-982fed1ec67c TASK_PLAN_FILE=.local/tasks/aa4227c8-a7e9-4c86-a6e6-982fed1ec67c.md npm run gate:run -- --id aa4227c8-a7e9-4c86-a6e6-982fed1ec67c --tier test-standard
**Do not switch tiers:** This task ID is strictly bound to this tier. Other tiers will block execution; changes require a supported amendment.

## Planned guard assertions
- R1 request ownership — Both production routes reject forged foreign, wrong-photo, missing and malformed pin IDs before provider work and leave victim results unchanged.
- R2 persistence isolation — The production storage method rejects mismatched pin/photo/session relationships and foreign conflict rows without changing any rows in a mixed batch.
- R3 valid scans — Valid same-scope inserts and updates succeed; valid editor access remains accepted.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** R1 client-controlled pin IDs in both endpoints; R2 database insert and conflict update isolation plus atomic batch rollback; R3 authorized scanning compatibility
**Test location:** server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — label scan object authorization HTTP and PostgreSQL cases
**What it checks:** Send forged pin IDs through actual production routes and assert rejection and unchanged victim data; call actual storage with invalid ownership and foreign conflicts and assert rejection plus batch rollback; assert normal inserts and updates succeed.

# Enforce label scan pin, photo and session ownership

## Task identity
**Task ID:** aa4227c8-a7e9-4c86-a6e6-982fed1ec67c
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** 1c473ac807c45b104d7ca36fd94163ae3d0d4d4e97dbb5dd71bc8a81b98a6736

## Scope
Repair the assigned label scan BOLA in both production analyze-labels routes and upsertScanResults. Reject missing, malformed or mismatched pin/photo/session identifiers before image/provider work; protect persistence against mismatched ownership and foreign conflict rows, atomically. Preserve valid scanning, collaborator access, provider and UI flows. No schema changes.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3

**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** Fixes a persistent cross-session data-integrity and object-authorization vulnerability.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Assigned task 1012 in the active conversation
**Owner direction:** Patch cross-session label scan result overwrites without new product flows
**Applicability:** Route and persistence security hardening and regression coverage are within assigned scope; independent verification not selected

None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Flaky-test rule:** A passing retry establishes intermittency, not pre-existing provenance.

**Why:** The backend authorization repair needs compiler checks, executable production-route regressions and real PostgreSQL persistence coverage.

# Enforce label scan pin, photo and session ownership

## Task identity
**Task ID:** aa4227c8-a7e9-4c86-a6e6-982fed1ec67c
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** 1c473ac807c45b104d7ca36fd94163ae3d0d4d4e97dbb5dd71bc8a81b98a6736

## Scope
Repair the assigned label scan BOLA in both production analyze-labels routes and upsertScanResults. Reject missing, malformed or mismatched pin/photo/session identifiers before image/provider work; protect persistence against mismatched ownership and foreign conflict rows, atomically. Preserve valid scanning, collaborator access, provider and UI flows. No schema changes.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** Fixes a persistent cross-session data-integrity and object-authorization vulnerability.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Assigned task 1012 in the active conversation
**Owner direction:** Patch cross-session label scan result overwrites without new product flows
**Applicability:** Route and persistence security hardening and regression coverage are within assigned scope; independent verification not selected

## Pre-existing failures to ignore
None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Flaky-test rule:** A passing retry establishes intermittency, not pre-existing provenance.

## Validation
**Command:** `test-standard`
**Why:** The backend authorization repair needs compiler checks, executable production-route regressions and real PostgreSQL persistence coverage.
**Coverage evidence:** docs/validation/manifest.json; docs/validation/manifest.json test-standard typecheck and unit-tests include server/__tests__/routes.test.ts, where HTTP and isolated PostgreSQL regression cases run.; supported invocation: TASK_ID=aa4227c8-a7e9-4c86-a6e6-982fed1ec67c TASK_PLAN_FILE=.local/tasks/aa4227c8-a7e9-4c86-a6e6-982fed1ec67c.md npm run gate:run -- --id aa4227c8-a7e9-4c86-a6e6-982fed1ec67c --tier test-standard
**Do not switch tiers:** This task ID is strictly bound to this tier. Other tiers will block execution; changes require a supported amendment.

## Planned guard assertions
- R1 request ownership — Both production routes reject forged foreign, wrong-photo, missing and malformed pin IDs before provider work and leave victim results unchanged.
- R2 persistence isolation — The production storage method rejects mismatched pin/photo/session relationships and foreign conflict rows without changing any rows in a mixed batch.
- R3 valid scans — Valid same-scope inserts and updates succeed; valid editor access remains accepted.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** R1 client-controlled pin IDs in both endpoints; R2 database insert and conflict update isolation plus atomic batch rollback; R3 authorized scanning compatibility
**Test location:** server/__tests__/routes.test.ts — label scan object authorization HTTP and PostgreSQL cases
**What it checks:** Send forged pin IDs through actual production routes and assert rejection and unchanged victim data; call actual storage with invalid ownership and foreign conflicts and assert rejection plus batch rollback; assert normal inserts and updates succeed.

## Task identity

**Revision:** 1

## Scope
Repair the assigned label scan BOLA in both production analyze-labels routes and upsertScanResults. Preserve valid scanning, collaborator access, provider and UI flows. No schema changes.

## Task identity
**Task ID:** aa4227c8-a7e9-4c86-a6e6-982fed1ec67c
**Revision:** 1
**Skill pin:** 1c473ac807c45b104d7ca36fd94163ae3d0d4d4e97dbb5dd71bc8a81b98a6736

## Scope
Repair the assigned label scan BOLA in both production analyze-labels routes and upsertScanResults. Preserve valid scanning, collaborator access, provider and UI flows. No schema changes.

**Reference:** Assigned task 1012 in the active conversation
**Owner direction:** Patch cross-session label scan result overwrites without new product flows
**Applicability:** Route and persistence security hardening and regression coverage are within assigned scope; independent verification not selected

None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

Repair the assigned label scan BOLA in both production analyze-labels routes and upsertScanResults. # Repair reviewed release schema fingerprint

## Task identity
**Task ID:** 8255f524-e4dd-4b79-8094-cfa274957434
**Revision:** 2
**Skill pin:** 1c473ac807c45b104d7ca36fd94163ae3d0d4d4e97dbb5dd71bc8a81b98a6736

## Scope
Execute the approved native task 1014 plan: reproduce the release-schema-contract mismatch using the bound diagnostic; review current export and prior candidate metadata including all columns/defaults/indexes/roles/legacy objects; obtain publication metadata read-only via supported configuration and canonicalize both endpoints; update only justified transition pins and review records. Preserve exact-pair fail-closed behavior and current-schema acceptance. Add missing assertions for nullable integer folders.trashed_from_parent_folder_id and independent metadata mutations; prove run-owned database isolation/cleanup. User-approved extension: minimally update Multer from vulnerable 2.4.0 to compatible patched 2.5.0 for GHSA-q7qp-rjg7-q26m, raise installed/lockfile version guards with vulnerable-version negative controls, and test delayed asynchronous fileFilter callback after request teardown plus existing image-upload compatibility. Do not redesign upload architecture or change upload runtime policy. No publishing, schema push, production DDL/data changes, workload/policy changes, auth migration membership changes, or other unrelated repairs. If endpoint review is unavailable, report BLOCKED rather than replace hashes blindly. Finish focused diagnostics then complete heavy workload and revision-bound R1/R2/R3/R4 handoff; separate review not selected.

## Regression classification
**Guard contract:** 1e19c766f4eb453d7a123df93a10ea43925dc520a10f6fa078b9143d1d2bf4a3
**Form:** normal
**Material scope:** true
**Rationale:** The accepted schema transition is material compatibility/data integrity; Multer security upgrading is material upload security, reliability and lifecycle compatibility. Both changed boundaries need concrete detecting assertions.

## Approval evidence
**Reference:** Current native task 1014 plus user answer Include the security update (recommended) to the Multer scope-extension question
**Owner direction:** Repair the reviewed schema fingerprint and include the minimal Multer security update so full validation can proceed
**Applicability:** User explicitly authorized the security extension after the heavy security-audit failure; all other exclusions and the sole bound test-heavy tier remain unchanged

## Pre-existing failures to ignore
None known at plan time. Treat every failure as a potential regression.

**Flaky-test rule:** A passing retry establishes intermittency, not pre-existing provenance.

## Validation
**Command:** `test-heavy`
**Why:** The reported completion failure belongs to the heavy workload; only the full heavy run establishes end-to-end repair.
**Coverage evidence:** docs/validation/manifest.json; docs/validation/manifest.json test-heavy 900000ms: release-schema-contract exports and executes isolated PostgreSQL metadata, startup-smoke and startup-smoke-boundaries cover initialization, schema-check validates migrations, plus all retained unit/browser and harness steps. Use gate:run --tier test-heavy --step release-schema-contract for diagnostics and unfiltered gate:run --tier test-heavy for completion.; supported invocation: TASK_ID=8255f524-e4dd-4b79-8094-cfa274957434 TASK_PLAN_FILE=.local/tasks/8255f524-e4dd-4b79-8094-cfa274957434.md npm run gate:run -- --id 8255f524-e4dd-4b79-8094-cfa274957434 --tier test-heavy
**Do not switch tiers:** This task ID is strictly bound to this tier. Other tiers will block execution; changes require a supported amendment.

## Planned guard assertions
- R1 candidate parity — Real Drizzle export and reviewed migration execution includes folders.trashed_from_parent_folder_id as nullable integer with no default and equals the explicitly reviewed candidate fingerprint.
- R2 transition exactness — Application canonicalizer establishes both reviewed endpoints; current equality and exact pair pass, independently changed candidate and publication metadata reject with target-drift.
- R3 database isolation and cleanup — Existing owned-target lifecycle and overlap guards reject unsafe targets, permit only owned disposable DDL, and demonstrate cleanup without publication mutation.
- R4 patched upload lifecycle — Installed and locked Multer satisfy the 2.5.0 floor, negative controls reject 2.4.0; a real HTTP request is torn down while fileFilter is pending, delayed acceptance cannot reach storage or persistence, the process remains responsive, and existing supported-image/limit/malformed/abort upload tests pass.

## Regression Guard
**Covers:** R1 stale candidate pin; R2 broadened endpoint acceptance; R3 unowned database mutation/leak; R4 vulnerable Multer regression, post-teardown delayed filter acceptance, and upload-policy compatibility.
**Test location:** scripts/__tests__/release-schema-preflight.test.mjs — real schema and exact-pair mutation controls; scripts/__tests__/managed-clerk-release.test.mjs — owned lifecycle; server/__tests__/dependency-media-security.test.ts — delayed-filter teardown and image upload cases; scripts/__tests__/dependency-tooling-security.test.mjs — Multer floor/negative controls
**What it checks:** R1 exact exported column and old/new hashes; R2 exact reviewed pair/current equality pass and changed endpoints reject; R3 overlap refuses and owned target disappears; R4 floor rejects Multer 2.4.0 and actual delayed-filter teardown never reaches storage/persistence, does not crash/hang the process, and subsequent valid uploads still work.
